docs.title: Translating NodeMT4 docs
docs.text: The docs are internationalised with mkdocs-static-i18n (suffix structure). English is the source; 27 target languages are configured. This page is the skeleton for translators.

docs.title: How it works (the mechanism)
docs.text:
• Language switcher — the globe menu in the header lists every configured language; it's generated automatically from the plugin config in mkdocs.yml.
  • Fallback — a page with no translation falls back to English, so every language already works end-to-end. You translate pages one at a time; nothing breaks in the meantime.
  • URLs — English is at the root (/NodeMT4/…), each language under its locale (/NodeMT4/zh/…, /NodeMT4/ja/…, …).

You don't pre-create blank files for every page — that would hide the English fallback behind empty pages. Create a translation file only when you actually translate that page.

docs.title: How to translate a page
docs.text:
Suffix structure: put the translation next to the English file, with the locale before .md.

docs/All_Guides/GETTING_STARTED.md        # English (source)
docs/All_Guides/GETTING_STARTED.zh.md     # 简体中文
docs/All_Guides/GETTING_STARTED.ja.md     # 日本語
docs/index.md                             # English home
docs/index.ja.md                          # 日本語 home

Steps:

  1. Copy the English page.md to page.<locale>.md.
  2. Translate the prose. Keep unchanged: code blocks, API names, enum constants, file paths, links, and front-matter keys (hide:, description:).
  3. Build (python -m mkdocs build) or serve (python -m mkdocs serve) and check the page under /<locale>/.

Translate in this order (highest value first): index → All_Guides/GETTING_STARTED → MT4_For_Beginners → Your_First_Project → GLOSSARY → RETURN_CODES_REFERENCE, then the rest. The deep API/method pages are read mostly in English and can come last.

docs.title: Right-to-left languages
docs.text: ar, fa, ur, he are configured with direction: rtl — the theme flips layout automatically for those locales. Keep code/paths LTR (Markdown handles this).

docs.title: The Concurrency Model — How NodeMT4 Executes
docs.text: NodeMT4 is built on Promises and async/await. Unary calls are async functions you await; streams hand you a callback plus a Subscription you cancel. Everything runs on Node's single-threaded event loop — no threads, no locks.

docs.title: 🎯 Two shapes of call
docs.text: Shape What it is How you consume it Unary (request / response) getAccountInfo(), quote(), orderSend() await it; the promise resolves with the result (or rejects) Server stream onSymbolTick(), subscribeQuotes() pass a callback; it fires per payload; keep the returned Subscription and call unsubscribe()

docs.title: Unary — await
docs.text:
Every unary method returns a Promise. There is nothing to poll; the gRPC round-trip happens inside the await.

const a = await service.getAccountInfo();     // resolves with AccountInfo
console.log(a.balance, a.equity);

const quote = await service.quote('EURUSD');  // Quote

A failure rejects the promise with an MrpcError (or a TradeOutcomeUnknownError for a trade) — catch it:

try {
  const ticket = await sugar.buyMarket('EURUSD', 0.10);
} catch (e) {
  console.error('rejected:', e.message);
}

docs.title: Streaming — callback + Subscription
docs.text:
A stream does not return data; it calls your callback on each payload and returns a handle to stop it.

const sub = service.subscribeQuotes(['EURUSD'], (t) => {
  console.log(t.bid, t.ask);
}, (err) => console.error(err.message));

setTimeout(() => sub.unsubscribe(), 30_000);   // stop after 30s

docs.title: 🧵 One event loop, no threads
docs.text:
Node runs your JavaScript on one thread. await doesn't spawn a thread — it yields the event loop until the I/O completes, then resumes. That means:

  • No data races on your own variables within a synchronous run — but another callback or timer can run between your awaits. Don't assume state is unchanged across an await.
  • A long synchronous loop blocks everything (including stream callbacks). Keep callbacks short; offload heavy CPU work.
  • Stream callbacks are invoked as payloads arrive, interleaved with your unary awaits on the same loop.

docs.title: 🔀 Running calls concurrently
docs.text:
await in sequence is serial. To run independent calls at once, start them together and Promise.all:

// serial — two round-trips back to back
const bid = await sugar.getBid('EURUSD');
const ask = await sugar.getAsk('EURUSD');

// concurrent — both in flight together
const [b, a] = await Promise.all([
  sugar.getBid('EURUSD'),
  sugar.getAsk('EURUSD'),
]);

The SDK itself does this internally — e.g. getPriceInfo fetches the quote and the symbol params with Promise.all.

docs.title: ⏱️ Timeouts
docs.text:
Every unary call carries an internal gRPC deadline; on expiry the promise rejects.

  • Default deadline — 30_000 ms. Set on MT4Account.callTimeoutMs; tune it for a slow link:
sugar.account().callTimeoutMs = 60_000;   // 60s for every unary call
  • Per-call deadlines. Some calls use a longer internal deadline — the history reads quoteHistory / ordersHistory and the equity-curve stats (tradeStatsEquityHistory / equityHistory) use 60 s, symbolParamsMany with no name (all symbols) up to 120 s, and every trade call (orderSend / orderModify / orderCloseDelete / orderCloseBy) uses 60 s. (accountSummary / serverTimezone are quick 15 s reads.)
  • Connect takes timeoutSeconds in its options (default 60); the gRPC deadline is set a little longer so it outlives the gateway's own terminal start-up.
  • MT4Sugar manages timeouts for you — its methods take no timeout argument.

docs.title: 🧹 Lifecycle
docs.text:
const sugar = MT4Sugar.create('mt4.mrpc.pro', 443, apiKey);
await sugar.quickConnect(login, password, server);   // obtains the terminal session
// … use it …
await sugar.service().disconnect(true);              // stop the terminal + free resources

Always unsubscribe streams and disconnect when done — an open stream or warm terminal keeps resources alive on the gateway (a trial allows one terminal per IP).

docs.title: Enums Usage Reference — Node
docs.text: The generated protobuf enums are plain JavaScript namespace objects: Namespace.CONSTANT → number. This page shows which namespace holds which enum, and how to use them at each layer.

docs.title: 🧭 How protobuf enums look in Node
docs.text:
import { TradingHelperPb } from '@metarpc/nodemt4';

TradingHelperPb.OrderSendOperationType.OC_OP_BUY   // === 0 (a number)

Each *Pb module is re-exported from the package. An enum is an object mapping names to numbers; you pass the value into a setter or compare it against a getter.

MT4 is simpler than MT5 here. MT4 has no per-property symbol enums (SymbolInfoDouble/Integer/String) — a symbol's fields come back as a flat SymbolParams struct, so you rarely need an enum at all. The ones that matter are the order type, the timeframe, the sort modes and the account trade mode.

docs.title: 📇 The enums you'll use most
docs.text:
Enum Namespace Example value Order type (send) TradingHelperPb.OrderSendOperationType OC_OP_BUY (0) Open order type AccountHelperPb.OpenedOrderType 0 BUY … 5 SELL_STOP Account trade mode AccountHelperPb.EnumAccountTradeMode ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_DEMO (0) Opened-orders sort AccountHelperPb.EnumOpenedOrderSortType SORT_BY_OPEN_TIME_DESC (1) History sort AccountHelperPb.EnumOrderHistorySortType HISTORY_SORT_BY_CLOSE_TIME_DESC (3) Quote-history timeframe MarketInfoPb.ENUM_QUOTE_HISTORY_TIMEFRAME M1 … MN1 — or use the TIMEFRAMES map MT4 error number ErrorPb.MqlErrorCode 130 invalid stops, 134 no money gRPC error type ErrorPb.ErrorType MRPC_TIMEOUT, TERMINAL_API_TIMEOUT

Namespaces follow the proto service the message belongs to. When unsure, open the stub (package/*_pb.js) or use the Protobuf Inspector.

docs.title: 🔽 Low level (MT4Account) — pass the enum directly
docs.text:
import { MT4Account, TradingHelperPb } from '@metarpc/nodemt4';

const req = new TradingHelperPb.OrderSendRequest();
req.setSymbol('EURUSD');
req.setOperationType(TradingHelperPb.OrderSendOperationType.OC_OP_BUY);  // the enum value
req.setVolume(0.01);
req.setPrice(ask);
await account.orderSend(req);

docs.title: 🟦 Mid level (MT4Service) — string action instead of the enum
docs.text:
// 'BUY' / 'SELL' / 'BUY_LIMIT' / 'SELL_LIMIT' / 'BUY_STOP' / 'SELL_STOP' → mapped to OrderSendOperationType
await service.orderSend({ symbol: 'EURUSD', cmd: 'BUY', lots: 0.01 });

docs.title: 🟩 High level (MT4Sugar) — enums hidden
docs.text:
The sugar layer wraps the common operations so you never touch an enum:

await sugar.buyMarket('EURUSD', 0.01);      // OC_OP_BUY inside
const digits = await sugar.getSymbolDigits('EURUSD');   // reads SymbolParams.digits — no enum

docs.title: 🛒 Order-type enum (trading)
docs.text:
OC_OP_BUY = 0   OC_OP_SELL = 1   OC_OP_BUYLIMIT = 2
OC_OP_SELLLIMIT = 3   OC_OP_BUYSTOP = 4   OC_OP_SELLSTOP = 5

The friendly layers accept the string action instead — 'BUY', 'SELL_LIMIT', … — and map it to this enum for you (MT4Service.orderSend, MT4Sugar.buyMarket / buyLimit / …). Open orders report the same 0–5 numbering in OrderInfo.type (AccountHelperPb.OpenedOrderType).

docs.title: ⏱️ Timeframe enum (quote history)
docs.text:
quoteHistory takes a timeframe ordinal, not minutes. Use the exported TIMEFRAMES map:

import { TIMEFRAMES } from '@metarpc/nodemt4';
// M1=0 M5=1 M15=2 M30=3 H1=4 H4=5 D1=6 W1=7 MN1=8
req.setTimeframe(TIMEFRAMES['H1']);   // 4

The friendly layers accept the string directly: service.quoteHistory('EURUSD', 'H1', from, to) / service.lastBars('EURUSD', 'H1', 100).

docs.title: 📒 Complete enum catalog
docs.text: The SDK reaches enums through the *Pb namespaces it re-exports — ConnectionPb, AccountHelperPb, TradingHelperPb, SubscriptionsPb, MarketInfoPb, TradeStatsPb, ServerTimezonePb, ErrorPb. 19 enums are reachable this way. Import each from its home namespace below — many are also available from the namespaces that transitively require it, but the home namespace always works.

docs.title: Trading — TradingHelperPb
docs.text: Enum Values Use OrderSendOperationType 6 Order type for orderSend (0–5). OrderCloseDeleteMode 2 Result mode of orderCloseDelete (0 close · 1 delete).

docs.title: Account & symbols — AccountHelperPb
docs.text: Enum Values Use OpenedOrderType 8 Type of an open/pending order (0–5 trade; 6–7 balance/credit). EnumAccountTradeMode 3 DEMO (0) / CONTEST (1) / REAL (2). EnumAccountMarginMode 3 Margin mode. EnumOpenedOrderSortType 4 openedOrders ordering. EnumOrderHistorySortType 6 ordersHistory ordering. SP_ENUM_SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE 5 Symbol trade mode. SP_ENUM_SYMBOL_TRADE_EXECUTION 4 Symbol execution mode. SP_ENUM_TRADE_CALC_MODE 3 Symbol margin-calc mode.

docs.title: Market & quotes — MarketInfoPb
docs.text: Enum Values Use ENUM_QUOTE_HISTORY_TIMEFRAME 9 Timeframe for quoteHistory (see TIMEFRAMES).

docs.title: Streaming — SubscriptionsPb
docs.text: Enum Values Use SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE 6 Order type in trade-event payloads. MT4_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE 2 Event group in onTrade.

docs.title: Connection — ConnectionPb
docs.text: Enum Values Use ProxyTypes 4 Proxy type for a connect. TerminalType 2 Terminal type.

docs.title: Server timezone — ServerTimezonePb
docs.text: Enum Values Use SERVER_TIMEZONE_SOURCE 3 Source of the server-timezone offset.

docs.title: Errors — ErrorPb
docs.text:
Enum Values Use MqlErrorCode 112 The MT4 error numbers (mqlIntCode). See Return Codes. ErrorType 10 gRPC/gateway error type (MRPC_TIMEOUT, TERMINAL_API_TIMEOUT, …). LogType 3 Log severity.

Not re-exported by the SDK. The raw package/*_pb.js stubs also define GUI / chart / legacy enums (GuiFormFieldType, GuiTwoFactorType, ChartTemplateMode, QUOTE_HISTORY_TIMEFRAME) whose stub modules this SDK does not export — they aren't needed for trading. If you need them, require the raw stub directly or use the Protobuf Inspector.

Discover values at runtime with the Protobuf Inspector: node examples/demos/helpers/15_protobuf_inspector.js enum OrderSendOperationType.

docs.title: Getting Started with NodeMT4
docs.text: Quick setup — connect to MetaTrader 4 from Node.js in a few minutes.

docs.title: What is NodeMT4?
docs.text:
NodeMT4 is a Node.js / TypeScript client for MetaTrader 4 accounts over the MetaRPC gRPC API (mt4.mrpc.pro:443). It's organised in three layers you can mix freely:

  • MT4Account — raw gRPC, protobuf in/out, full control.
  • MT4Service — typed objects, plain arguments.
  • MT4Sugar — one-line helpers.

See the Project Map for how they fit together.

docs.title: Install & downloads
docs.text: Two ways to use NodeMT4 — take our ready-made project, or take only the protocol and build your own client.

docs.title: 1 · Take our project (recommended)
docs.text:
The complete thing we built: the three layers (MT4Sugar / MT4Service / MT4Account), the TypeScript types, and the generated stubs — all wired together.

  • Just the library, for your own app:
npm install github:MetaRPC/NodeMT4

Installs as @metarpc/nodemt4 with the SDK, the types, and the protobuf stubs under @metarpc/nodemt4/package/.

  • The full repo (adds the runnable examples/demos/ and the tests):
git clone https://github.com/MetaRPC/NodeMT4.git
cd NodeMT4
npm install
node examples/demos/main.js 6     # run a demo (6 = sugar basics)

The compiled src/*.js are checked in, so no build step is required (run npm run build only after editing the TypeScript).

🎓 New here? Start with the full repo (the git clone above). You get all three layers side by side (MT4Account → MT4Service → MT4Sugar) and ready-made examples written on each of them that you can run and read. Learn the SDK this way first — only once you're comfortable should you consider building your own from the raw protos (option 2 below).

docs.title: 2 · Take only the protos and build it yourself (raw gRPC)
docs.text:
For advanced use — after you know the SDK. Skip our layers and talk to the gateway from the generated stubs directly. The stubs ship in the package/ folder (mt4-term-api-*_pb.js, *_grpc_pb.js, and the google/ subfolder).

Download just the package/ folder (not the whole repo) — any of these:

# A) quickest — grab only the subfolder (no git history)
npx degit MetaRPC/NodeMT4/package package

# B) pure git — sparse-checkout only package/
git clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --no-checkout https://github.com/MetaRPC/NodeMT4.git
cd NodeMT4 && git sparse-checkout set --no-cone 'package/**' && git checkout

# C) via npm — then copy the folder out of node_modules
npm install github:MetaRPC/NodeMT4
cp -r node_modules/@metarpc/nodemt4/package ./package

Then install the gRPC + protobuf runtime next to it:

npm install google-protobuf @grpc/grpc-js

The raw .proto sources (to regenerate stubs for another language or version) are on the MT4 Client API Explorer → Download MT4 Protos.

⚠️ The stubs are not standalone — take the whole package/ folder, not single files. Each *_pb.js cross-requires its siblings (e.g. ./mrpc-mt4-error_pb.js), the ./google/ subfolder and google-protobuf. This path gives you raw gRPC with no 3-layer SDK — see the Protobuf Inspector.

docs.title: 🔑 API Key & Authentication
docs.text:
Connecting to the MetaRPC production endpoint (mt4.mrpc.pro:443) uses a personal API key — you get one just by registering on our site:

  1. Sign up — create a free account at https://mrpc.pro/signup.
  2. Copy your key — it's provisioned automatically; open the MT4 Client API Explorer and your key is shown at the top (Active · Copy key). Nothing to generate — the key itself is free.
  3. Use it — pass the key to MT4Sugar.create(host, port, apiKey) (or set the MRPC_API_KEY environment variable instead of hard-coding it).

You'll also need an MT4 demo account (login / password / server, e.g. TeleTrade-Demo) — see MT4 for Beginners to create one (one click for $1, or free via the MT4 terminal).

💡 TRIAL / keyless. No key yet? Pass the literal value TRIAL as the key to connect for a first look. Your own key — free from sign-up — is for normal use.

docs.title: 🆔 Session ID is automatic
docs.text: You never call GetId or supply an id header. On connect / connectEx the server generates a terminal session GUID (terminalInstanceGuid) and the SDK attaches it — alongside your API key — to every later request and stream automatically.

docs.title: Connect & read the account
docs.text:
import { MT4Sugar } from '@metarpc/nodemt4';

const sugar = MT4Sugar.create('mt4.mrpc.pro', 443, 'YOUR_API_KEY');
await sugar.quickConnect(500000, 'password', 'TeleTrade-Demo');

const info = await sugar.getAccountInfo();
console.log(`${info.name} #${info.login} — ${info.balance} ${info.currency} on ${info.server}`);

Prefer environment variables? Set MT4_LOGIN / MT4_PASSWORD / MT4_SERVER and call sugar.quickConnect() with no arguments.

docs.title: A first trade (demo)
docs.text:
const ticket = await sugar.buyMarket('EURUSD', 0.01);   // tiny demo order
console.log('opened #', ticket);
await sugar.closePosition(ticket);

Trading helpers throw MrpcError on a broker rejection (and TradeOutcomeUnknownError when an outcome is unknown) — wrap them in try/catch. See Return Codes & the error model.

On MT4 a "position" is an open market order (one ticket per fill, no netting).

docs.title: Dropping down a layer
docs.text:
Need something the sugar layer doesn't expose? Go down:

const service = sugar.service();   // MT4Service — typed objects
const account = sugar.account();   // MT4Account — raw protobuf

const quote = await service.quote('EURUSD');   // Quote { bid, ask, time }
// const raw = await account.quote(req);        // raw QuoteData (build the request yourself)

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: The MT4, trading and SDK terms you'll meet in these docs, grouped by kind.

docs.title: 🏗️ Architectural terms
docs.text:
Three-layer architecture — the SDK is three decoupled layers, each owning the one below (sugar.service() → MT4Service, service.account() → MT4Account). See the Project Map.

MT4Account — the low-level layer. Raw gRPC: you pass protobuf *Request messages and read *Data replies with getXxx() getters. Owns the channel, the gRPC clients, auth metadata, reconnect and streaming. → overview

MT4Service — the mid layer. Same calls, but it builds the protobuf from plain arguments and returns typed objects (AccountInfo, Quote, OrderInfo…). → overview

MT4Sugar — the high layer. One-line helpers (buyMarket, closeAllPositions) with smart defaults; throws on failure. → overview

DTO — "data transfer object": the plain TypeScript interfaces MT4Service returns instead of protobuf (AccountInfo, Quote, OrderInfo, SymbolParams, Bar, TradeStats…).

MrpcError — the error thrown when the gateway or terminal reports a problem. Carries code, message, and for trade rejections the MT4 error number mqlIntCode / mqlDescription. Flags: isInvalidLogin (never retry), isTerminalLost (reconnect), isApiKeyError, isTradeOutcomeUnknown. Alias: MT4Error. See Return Codes → the error object.

TradeOutcomeUnknownError — thrown when a trade call's transport fails after the request may have reached the terminal (or MT4 answers 128 timeout). The trade is never re-sent — reconcile with openedOrders(). See Return Codes.

Subscription — what a streaming method returns: { unsubscribe(): void }. Call unsubscribe() to stop the stream.

docs.title: 🧩 Node / TypeScript-specific concepts
docs.text:
Async / await — every network call returns a Promise; await it inside async functions and wrap in try/catch.

const sugar = MT4Sugar.create('mt4.mrpc.pro', 443, process.env.MRPC_API_KEY);
await sugar.quickConnect(login, 'password', 'TeleTrade-Demo');
const balance = await sugar.getBalance();

Promise.all for parallel reads — independent calls run concurrently instead of one-by-one.

const [quote, params] = await Promise.all([
  service.quote('EURUSD'),
  service.symbolParams('EURUSD'),
]);

Typed objects vs protobuf stubs — the low layer returns generated protobuf objects (reply.getXxx()); the mid layer unwraps them into typed DTOs. The stubs are typed any, so discover real names with the Protobuf Inspector.

const d = await account.openedOrders();        // low: protobuf, d.getOrderInfosList()
const orders = await service.openedOrders();   // mid: typed OrderInfo[]

Streaming — the Subscription/callback model — a streaming method returns a Subscription and invokes your callback per payload; errors go to the optional onError. Always unsubscribe() when done. See gRPC Stream Management.

const sub = service.subscribeQuotes(['EURUSD'], (t) => console.log(t.bid, t.ask));
// later:
sub.unsubscribe();

Connection & cleanup — connect / quickConnect opens the terminal session; disconnect(true) closes it and frees the terminal (a trial allows one per IP). Use try/finally.

try { /* … */ } finally { await sugar.service().disconnect(true); }

docs.title: Account
docs.text:
Balance — closed-trade money; excludes floating P/L. Equity — balance + floating P/L; moves with open orders. Margin — funds locked to hold orders. Free margin — equity − margin; available to open more. Margin level — equity / margin × 100 (%); low levels risk a stop-out. Leverage — the multiplier (1:100) setting margin need. Trade mode — DEMO, CONTEST or REAL.

On MT4, margin / free margin / margin level aren't in the account summary — read them from a live OnOpenedOrdersProfit snapshot (MT4Sugar.getMargin() / getFreeMargin() / getMarginLevel()).

docs.title: Instruments & prices
docs.text: Symbol — a tradable instrument (EURUSD, XAUUSD). Bid / Ask — sell / buy price; spread = ask − bid. Digits — decimal places (5 for EURUSD, 3 for JPY). Tick — one price update (quote / onSymbolTick). Server time — every MT4 timestamp is broker time; convert with serverTimezone() or AccountInfo.utcServerShiftMinutes.

docs.title: Orders & history (MT4 model)
docs.text: Order — an instruction to trade. Market fills now; pending (LIMIT/STOP) waits for a price. Ticket — the numeric id that addresses every order. Order type (OrderSendOperationType): OC_OP_BUY=0, OC_OP_SELL=1, OC_OP_BUYLIMIT=2, OC_OP_SELLLIMIT=3, OC_OP_BUYSTOP=4, OC_OP_SELLSTOP=5. No positions, no netting — MT4 keeps each fill as its own order; the friendly layers call open market orders (types 0/1) "positions" for convenience. History order — a closed order (with a close time and close price). SL / TP — stop-loss / take-profit auto-close levels. Magic number — a client id tagging a strategy's orders. mqlIntCode — the MT4 error number a refusal carries (130 invalid stops, 131 invalid volume, 132 market closed, 134 no money, 138 requote, 128 trade timeout). See Return Codes.

docs.title: 📦 Technical concepts
docs.text:
Point — the smallest price increment (0.00001 on 5-digit EURUSD). Pip — the conventional move unit; in this SDK pip = point × (digits is 3 or 5 ? 10 : 1), so one pip on EURUSD = 0.0001. Tick value / tick size — the money value of one tick, and the price change one tick represents — inputs for P&L and sizing.

Lot / volume — trade size in lots (0.01 = micro). Must obey volume limits (volumeMin / volumeMax / volumeStep). Contract size — units of the base instrument per 1.0 lot.

Risk-based sizing — picking the lot so a stop of N pips loses a fixed % of balance: calculatePositionSize(symbol, riskPercent, stopLossPips). Risk amount = balance × riskPercent / 100. Required margin — margin a prospective order needs. Drawdown — the drop from a peak to current equity, %.

Stops level (SymbolParams.stopsLevel) — minimum distance, in points, SL/TP may sit from the market; closer → mqlIntCode 130.

Trailing stop — a stop that ratchets in your favour, never back (orchestrator). Breakeven — moving the stop to entry once in profit. Hedging — on MT4 you can always hold BUY and SELL on one symbol at once (no netting). Grid trading — bracketing price with pending orders (orchestrator). Scalping — many small short-lived trades. News trading — trading around releases; expect wide spreads / rejections. Kill-switch — close everything on a drawdown/margin breach (risk manager).

docs.title: 🔌 gRPC & protocol terms
docs.text:
gRPC — the RPC protocol the SDK speaks to mt4.mrpc.pro:443 (HTTP/2 + protobuf over TLS).

Protobuf — the binary message format. On the low layer you build *Request messages and read *Data replies with getXxx() getters; MT4Service hides this behind typed objects.

Streaming pattern — a server stream delivered via callback: a streaming method returns a Subscription and calls your callback per payload. See gRPC Stream Management.

Gateway — the MetaRPC service (mt4.mrpc.pro) bridging the SDK to MT4 terminals and managing sessions. Terminal — the MT4 instance your account runs on behind the gateway. Session / terminal instance guid — the id obtained on connect (ConnectEx), attached with your API key to every later call automatically. API key — your MetaRPC key; pass it to MT4Sugar.create(...), or use TRIAL.

docs.title: gRPC Stream Management — Node
docs.text: Every live feed in NodeMT4 is a gRPC server stream. The SDK wraps each one in the same simple contract: a callback per payload, an optional error callback, and a Subscription you must cancel. This page covers the contract, the lifecycle, and how to run streams safely.

docs.title: 🧰 The Subscription contract
docs.text:
interface Subscription { unsubscribe(): void; }

Every streaming method has the shape:

method(request, callback: (data) => void, onError?: (e: Error) => void): Subscription

import { SubscriptionsPb } from '@metarpc/nodemt4';

const req = new SubscriptionsPb.OnSymbolTickRequest();
req.setSymbolNamesList(['EURUSD']);

const sub = account.onSymbolTick(req, (data) => {
  const t = data.getSymbolTick();
  console.log(t.getSymbol(), t.getBid(), t.getAsk());
}, (err) => console.error('stream error:', err.message));

// stop it later — ALWAYS do this
sub.unsubscribe();

The friendly MT4Service variants take plain arguments and map the payload for you — e.g. service.subscribeQuotes(['EURUSD'], (tick) => …).

docs.title: 🔁 What happens under the hood
docs.text:
The low-level stream helper opens the gRPC server stream and forwards frames:

  • data frame → if the reply carries an error, your onError gets an MrpcError; otherwise your callback gets the reply's raw data (read it with getXxx()).
  • transport error → onError (unless you already unsubscribed and it's a CANCELLED).
  • stream end → if you didn't cancel it, onError receives MrpcError('… stream ended').
  • unsubscribe() → cancels the gRPC call; the resulting CANCELLED is swallowed, not surfaced.

So a clean shutdown is silent, and an unexpected end is reported.

docs.title: 📡 The streams available
docs.text:
Method (MT4Account) Mapped variant (MT4Service) Payload onSymbolTick(req, cb) subscribeQuotes(symbols, cb) → Tick ticks onTrade(req, cb) subscribeTrades(cb) trade events onOpenedOrdersProfit(req, cb) subscribeOpenedOrdersProfit(ms, cb) open orders + profit + account (margin), on a timer onOpenedOrdersTickets(req, cb) subscribeOpenedOrdersTickets(ms, cb) ticket snapshots, on a timer onConnectState(req, cb) subscribeConnectState(cb) terminal connection state

subscribeQuotes maps each tick to a friendly Tick; the others forward typed event objects (see MT4Service · Streaming).

docs.title: ⏲️ Timer-driven streams
docs.text:
onOpenedOrdersProfit and onOpenedOrdersTickets push on a timer you set in the request:

import { SubscriptionsPb } from '@metarpc/nodemt4';

const req = new SubscriptionsPb.OnOpenedOrdersProfitRequest();
req.setTimerPeriodMilliseconds(1000);   // every second

const sub = account.onOpenedOrdersProfit(req, (data) => {
  for (const o of data.getOpenedOrdersWithProfitUpdatedList()) {
    console.log(`#${o.getTicket()} ${o.getSymbol()}  ${o.getOrderProfit()}`);
  }
  const a = data.getAccountInfo();
  if (a) console.log('margin', a.getMargin());   // live margin lives here on MT4
});

This stream is also the reliable source of live margin on MT4 — MT4Sugar.getMargin() reads one snapshot of it.

docs.title: 🧹 Lifecycle & cleanup
docs.text:
• Keep the handle. Losing the Subscription means you can't stop the stream.
  • Unsubscribe on shutdown. Tie it to your app's teardown:
const subs = [];
subs.push(service.subscribeQuotes(['EURUSD'], onTick));
subs.push(service.subscribeTrades(onTrade));

process.on('SIGINT', () => {
  subs.forEach((s) => s.unsubscribe());
  process.exit(0);
});
  • Disconnect last. After unsubscribing, await sugar.service().disconnect() to release the terminal.

docs.title: ⚠️ Backpressure & long work
docs.text: Stream callbacks run on the single event loop (Concurrency Model). If a callback does heavy synchronous work, it stalls every other callback and timer. Keep callbacks light — push data into a queue and process it elsewhere if needed. Don't await a slow unary call inside a high-frequency tick callback without guarding against overlap.

docs.title: 🔌 Reconnection
docs.text: If the terminal drops, a stream ends and onError fires. To resume: reconnect the account (sugar.quickConnect(...) / account.reconnect()) and re-subscribe. The SDK does not silently auto-resubscribe a stream — you decide the policy (immediate retry, backoff, alert). The onConnectState stream is handy for gating on isConnected.

docs.title: MT4 for Beginners
docs.text: New to MetaTrader 4? This is the 5-minute mental model you need before the code makes sense.

docs.title: What MT4 is
docs.text:
MetaTrader 4 (MT4) is a trading platform. Your account lives on a broker's server (e.g. MetaQuotes-Demo or EGlobal-Demo). Through it you trade symbols (instruments like EURUSD or XAUUSD).

This SDK talks to your MT4 terminal over the network (gRPC to mt4.mrpc.pro:443) so you can automate everything from Node.js.

Always learn on a demo account. It trades with fake money on real prices — no risk.

docs.title: Getting a demo account & API key
docs.text:
Registration and your API key are free. Sign up at mrpc.pro/signup and your key is provisioned automatically — nothing to generate; in the web Explorer it's even attached to every call for you. What costs money is paid usage of the service (for example the instant $1 demo below).

To run the SDK you also need an MT4 demo account (login / password / server). You can get one two ways:

docs.title: ⚡ Fastest — one click on mrpc.pro ($1)
docs.text:
Our MT4 Client API Explorer (a live API playground) spins up a demo account instantly — no terminal install:

  1. Open the MT4 Client API Explorer (sign in first). Your API key is already shown under AUTHENTICATED API KEY (Active · Copy key).
  2. In the BROKER DEMO ACCOUNT panel pick a broker (the dropdown defaults to MetaQuotes-Demo) and click Open demo account ($1). The $1 is charged to your MetaRPC balance (the account that holds your API key) — not to a broker.
  3. The demo is created instantly with a ready login / password / server — you can even run real API calls right on that page (the key is attached automatically).

Copy the demo login / password / server, then jump to Getting Started to connect from Node.

docs.title: 🖥️ Free — create a demo in the MetaTrader 4 terminal
docs.text:
The no-cost route: create a demo account directly in the MT4 terminal (free), and connect with your free API key — or with the literal value TRIAL for a quick first look.

1 · Download & install MT4. Get the terminal from your broker, or the generic one from metatrader4.com/download, and install it.

2 · Find the Navigator panel. It's on the left, below Market Watch. Its Accounts section is where you add accounts.

3 · Open a new account. Right-click Accounts → Open an account to bring up the broker-server search.

4 · Pick a demo server. Find your broker's *-Demo (or MetaQuotes-Demo) and click Next.

5 · Choose "Open a new demo account" and click Next.

6 · Fill in the form (name, email; virtual deposit e.g. $10,000, leverage 1:100, currency USD), accept the terms, Next.

7 · Save your credentials. MT4 shows your login, password (master) and server. Copy them now — the SDK needs exactly these three values.

Two passwords are shown: the master password trades; the investor password is read-only. Use the master password with the SDK.

docs.title: The money words
docs.text:
Term In one line Balance Your settled money (no open trades counted). Equity Balance plus the profit/loss of trades you have open right now. Margin Money "reserved" while a trade is open. Free margin What's left to open new trades.

When you open a trade, equity moves tick by tick. When you close it, the result folds into balance.

⚠️ On MT4, margin isn't in the account summary. getBalance() / getEquity() are cheap reads; getMargin() / getFreeMargin() / getMarginLevel() take a quick live snapshot instead (see Balance & Margin).

docs.title: Buying and selling
docs.text:
• Buy (go long) — you profit if the price rises.
  • Sell (go short) — you profit if the price falls.

You trade in lots (volume). 0.01 is a micro lot — the smallest typical size, perfect for learning.

Two ways to enter:

  • Market order — fill now at the current price.
  • Pending order — wait for a price. A LIMIT waits for a better price; a STOP waits for a breakout.

docs.title: Protecting a trade
docs.text:
• Stop-Loss (SL) — auto-close if the price goes against you by so much. Caps the loss.
  • Take-Profit (TP) — auto-close once you've made your target.

Set them as prices, or let the SDK compute them from pip distances:

// 20-pip stop, 40-pip target, sized automatically
const lots = await sugar.calculatePositionSize('EURUSD', 1, 20);   // risk 1%
await sugar.buyMarketWithPips('EURUSD', lots, 20, 40);

docs.title: MT4's model: orders by ticket (no positions, no netting)
docs.text:
This is the big difference from MT5, so remember:

  • On MT4, everything is an order with a unique ticket number. A filled market BUY is just an open market order (type 0 BUY / 1 SELL); a pending order is a working instruction (types 2–5: LIMIT / STOP).
  • There are no "positions" as a separate concept and no netting — open two BUYs on EURUSD and you have two independent orders, each with its own ticket, not one merged position.
  • Closed orders move to history (with a close time and close price).

In this SDK the friendly layers call open market orders "positions" for convenience (getOpenPositions, closePosition), but under the hood they are MT4 orders addressed by ticket.

docs.title: Your first 10 lines
docs.text:
import { MT4Sugar } from '@metarpc/nodemt4';

const sugar = MT4Sugar.create('mt4.mrpc.pro', 443);
await sugar.quickConnect(login, 'password', 'MetaQuotes-Demo');

console.log('balance', await sugar.getBalance());
const ticket = await sugar.buyMarket('EURUSD', 0.01);   // tiny demo trade
await sugar.closePosition(ticket);

docs.title: Protobuf Inspector Guide — Node
docs.text:
The generated package/*_pb.js stubs are typed any, so TypeScript can't tell you a message's real getters, setters or enum names. This guide shows how to discover them at runtime — the fastest way to avoid "x.setPrice is not a function" surprises.

🛠️ Ready-made tool. The repo ships a runnable inspector — no need to write the snippets yourself:

node examples/demos/helpers/15_protobuf_inspector.js                        # interactive REPL
node examples/demos/helpers/15_protobuf_inspector.js OrderSendRequest       # one-shot: getters/setters
node examples/demos/helpers/15_protobuf_inspector.js enum OrderSendOperationType  # one-shot: enum values
node examples/demos/helpers/15_protobuf_inspector.js search Tick            # find message/enum names

It's offline (loads the stubs only — no connection, no key) and discovers 209 message types · 23 enums. REPL commands: list · <TypeName> · search <text> · enum <Name> · stats · help · exit. The techniques below are what it does under the hood.

docs.title: 🎯 Why you need it
docs.text:
• Field accessors aren't guessable. Repeated fields append List (getOrderInfosList); some getters are oddly cased or misspelled (getTradetickvalue, not getTradeTickValue; getCommision, with one s).
  • Request setters vary. OrderCloseDeleteRequest uses setOrderTicket / setLots / setClosingPrice.
  • Method name casing. The TradeStats client method is tradeUnrealizedPL (upper-case PL).
  • any typing hides all of it. The only source of truth is the stub — inspect it.

docs.title: 🔍 List a message's getters / setters
docs.text:
// node -e "...": print every getter of a message type
const Pb = require('@metarpc/nodemt4/package/mt4-term-api-trading-helper_pb');

const getters = Object.getOwnPropertyNames(Pb.OrderSendData.prototype).filter((n) => n.startsWith('get'));
const setters = Object.getOwnPropertyNames(Pb.OrderSendRequest.prototype).filter((n) => n.startsWith('set'));

console.log('getters:', getters.join(' '));
console.log('setters:', setters.join(' '));

Tip: the SDK re-exports these modules too — require('@metarpc/nodemt4').TradingHelperPb is the same object.

docs.title: 🧱 Find a message type by name
docs.text:
const Pb = require('@metarpc/nodemt4').SubscriptionsPb;

// which message types mention "Tick"?
console.log(Object.keys(Pb).filter((k) => /Tick/.test(k)));
// → [ 'OnSymbolTickData', 'OnSymbolTickReply', 'OnSymbolTickRequest', 'OnSymbolMqlTickInfo', ... ]

Then inspect the one you want with the getter/setter trick above.

docs.title: 🎛️ List an enum's values
docs.text:
const { TradingHelperPb } = require('@metarpc/nodemt4');

console.log(Object.entries(TradingHelperPb.OrderSendOperationType));
// → [ ['OC_OP_BUY',0], ['OC_OP_SELL',1], ['OC_OP_BUYLIMIT',2], ... ]

console.log(TradingHelperPb.OrderSendOperationType.OC_OP_BUYSTOP);  // the number (4)

To find which enums a namespace holds:

const ah = require('@metarpc/nodemt4').AccountHelperPb;
console.log(Object.keys(ah).filter((k) => /Enum|_ENUM_|Type/.test(k)));

docs.title: 🧪 Inspect a live reply
docs.text:
Log what the server actually returned — handy when a getter comes back empty:

const data = await account.accountSummary();
console.log(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(Object.getPrototypeOf(data)).filter((n) => n.startsWith('get')));
console.log('balance:', data.getAccountBalance());

A reply message also serialises: data.toObject() (where available) or data.serializeBinary() for the raw bytes.

docs.title: Return Codes & Error Handling
docs.text:
How errors surface in NodeMT4, the MT4 error numbers you'll meet, and the one rule that matters for trading: a trade is sent exactly once and never re-sent.

In NodeMT4 errors are exceptions — there are no error return values. Every call either resolves with its data or rejects. await inside try/catch.

import { MrpcError, TradeOutcomeUnknownError } from '@metarpc/nodemt4';

try {
  const res = await account.orderSend(req);
} catch (e) {
  if (e instanceof TradeOutcomeUnknownError) {
    // outcome unknown — reconcile, do NOT blindly resend
  } else if (e instanceof MrpcError) {
    console.log(e.code, e.mqlIntCode, e.mqlDescription);
  } else {
    // a raw gRPC transport error
  }
}

docs.title: 🧯 The error object — MrpcError
docs.text:
A server-side rejection (the reply carried an error) or a failed call surfaces as an MrpcError.

Member Type Meaning code string MRPC error code (e.g. API_KEY_INVALID, TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND, MQL4_EXECUTION_FAILED). message string Human-readable message. mqlIntCode number The MT4 error number (0 when not an MQL error). mqlDescription string The MT4 error text. operation string? For trade calls: OrderSend / OrderModify / OrderCloseDelete / OrderCloseBy.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Getter True when… Do isInvalidLogin INVALID_LOGIN / WRONG_PASSWORD / INVALID_ACCOUNT Never retry — brokers lock accounts. Fix credentials. isTerminalLost TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND / ..._REGISTRY_... await account.reconnect() and retry the read. isApiKeyError API_KEY_INVALID / API_KEY_REQUIRED Fix the key — retrying won't help. isTradeOutcomeUnknown a trade timed out / unknown transport outcome Reconcile with openedOrders() before any retry.

docs.title: ⚠️ TradeOutcomeUnknownError — the exactly-once rule
docs.text:
Every trade (orderSend / orderModify / orderCloseDelete / orderCloseBy) is sent once and never re-sent by the SDK. When the transport fails after the request may already have reached the terminal — gRPC UNAVAILABLE, DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, UNKNOWN, INTERNAL — or MT4 answers 128 (trade timeout), the call rejects with a TradeOutcomeUnknownError:

Member Meaning errorCode 'TRADE_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN' (same across every MetaRPC SDK). isTradeOutcomeUnknown true. operation The trade call (e.g. OrderSend). code / grpcCode The original gRPC status number (so err.code === grpc.status.UNAVAILABLE still works). details / metadata / cause The original gRPC error's fields.

The trade may or may not have executed. Check open orders (and recent history) before deciding whether to send it again. A refused API key inside a transport failure is not wrapped (the trade was refused, not lost).

docs.title: 📋 Common MT4 error numbers (mqlIntCode)
docs.text:
Code Name Meaning 0 ERR_NO_ERROR Success. 128 ERR_TRADE_TIMEOUT Trade timed out — outcome unknown (→ isTradeOutcomeUnknown). 129 ERR_INVALID_PRICE Invalid price. 130 ERR_INVALID_STOPS SL/TP too close to price (see SymbolParams.getTradestopslevel()). 131 ERR_INVALID_TRADE_VOLUME Volume not a valid multiple of the step / out of range. 132 ERR_MARKET_CLOSED Market is closed. 133 ERR_TRADE_DISABLED Trading disabled for the symbol/account. 134 ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_MONEY Insufficient free margin. 135 ERR_PRICE_CHANGED Price changed — re-quote and retry. 136 ERR_OFF_QUOTES No quotes available. 138 ERR_REQUOTE Broker re-quoted — retry at the new price. 139 ERR_ORDER_LOCKED Order is locked / being processed. 141 ERR_TOO_MANY_REQUESTS Slow down. 145 ERR_TRADE_MODIFY_DENIED Modification denied (too close to market). 146 ERR_TRADE_CONTEXT_BUSY Trade context busy — retry shortly. 148 ERR_TRADE_TOO_MANY_ORDERS Order count limit reached.

Codes 130/131/132/134/138 are refusals (MrpcError, not unknown-outcome). Code 128 and transport failures are unknown-outcome (TradeOutcomeUnknownError).

docs.title: 🌐 gRPC transport status (raw errors)
docs.text:
A transport failure (not a reply error) rejects with the gRPC error. The ones that make a trade outcome unknown:

gRPC status Typical cause UNAVAILABLE (14) Connection dropped / gateway unreachable. DEADLINE_EXCEEDED (4) The call outran its deadline. UNKNOWN (2) Unclassified server failure. INTERNAL (13) Internal gateway error.

For reads, the same transport errors are just the gRPC error — safe to retry.

docs.title: ✅ Handling recipe
docs.text:
import { MrpcError, TradeOutcomeUnknownError } from '@metarpc/nodemt4';

async function safeBuy(sugar, symbol, lots) {
  try {
    return await sugar.buyMarket(symbol, lots);
  } catch (e) {
    if (e instanceof TradeOutcomeUnknownError) {
      const open = await sugar.service().openedOrders();        // reconcile first
      // decide from `open` whether the order actually landed
      return null;
    }
    if (e instanceof MrpcError) {
      if (e.mqlIntCode === 134) console.log('not enough money');
      else if (e.mqlIntCode === 132) console.log('market closed');
      else console.log('refused:', e.code, e.mqlDescription);
      return null;
    }
    throw e;   // unexpected
  }
}

docs.title: The MetaRPC SDK family
docs.text:
Where NodeMT4 sits — and how it pairs with the Trade Copier to mirror a strategy across accounts.

MetaRPC ships two families of SDKs. They share the same authentication (ApiKey + owner user_key), the same gRPC-over-TLS transport to *.mrpc.pro, the same mrpc.pro portal and the same $1 demo onboarding — but they do different jobs.

Family Job Endpoint SDKs Terminal SDKs operate one trading account — connect, read, trade, stream mt4.mrpc.pro:443 (MT4) NodeMT4, GoMT4, CSharpMT4, CppMT4, RustMT4, PyMT4 (+ MT5 variants) Copier SDKs mirror trades between accounts (master → followers) copy.mrpc.pro:443 NodeCopier, GoCopier, CSharpCopier, PyCopier, …

NodeMT4 is a Terminal SDK. When you want to replicate what happens on one account to others, reach for the Copier SDK — in Node that's NodeCopier (@metarpc/nodecopier).

docs.title: How NodeMT4 and NodeCopier relate
docs.text:
NodeMT4 (this SDK) NodeCopier Scope one account a master → follower pair Does connect, quotes, orderSend, streams start · list · pause · remove a copier Endpoint mt4.mrpc.pro:443 copy.mrpc.pro:443 Thinks in ticks, orders by ticket risk sizing, pause/resume, copy logs

One sentence: NodeMT4 is where trades are produced and observed on an account; NodeCopier is how they're distributed to followers.

docs.title: The bridge — a shared terminal session
docs.text:
A copier's account carries an optional id — a terminal session GUID. That's exactly the value NodeMT4 obtains on connect: after connect / connectEx, the session GUID (terminalInstanceGuid) lives on account().id. So an account you're already running with NodeMT4 can be enrolled into a copier without reconnecting.

NodeCopier understands account type MT4 (plus MT5, cTrader CT, TradeLocker TL) — the same MRPC-hosted terminals NodeMT4 drives.

docs.title: End-to-end: run a strategy on the master, replicate to a follower
docs.text:
import { MT4Sugar } from '@metarpc/nodemt4';
import { CopierSugar } from '@metarpc/nodecopier';

const KEY = process.env.MRPC_API_KEY;   // owner key — note: TRIAL is NOT an owner key for the copier

// 1 · Operate the MASTER account with NodeMT4
const master = MT4Sugar.create('mt4.mrpc.pro', 443, KEY);
await master.quickConnect(Number(process.env.MASTER_LOGIN), process.env.MASTER_PASSWORD!, 'TeleTrade-Demo');
const masterSessionId = master.account().id;   // the ConnectEx terminal GUID → copier Account.id

// 2 · Start a copier: MASTER → FOLLOWER (NodeCopier, on copy.mrpc.pro)
await CopierSugar.create()
  .withCredentials(KEY!)
  .fromMaster({ type: 'MT4', user: Number(process.env.MASTER_LOGIN), password: process.env.MASTER_PASSWORD!, server: 'TeleTrade-Demo', id: masterSessionId! })
  .toSlave({ type: 'MT4', user: Number(process.env.SLAVE_LOGIN), password: process.env.SLAVE_PASSWORD!, server: 'TeleTrade-Demo' })
  .withLotMultiplier(1.0)   // or .withFixedLot(0.1)
  .withCopySl(true).withCopyTp(true)
  .start();

// 3 · Trades you now place on the master via NodeMT4 replicate to the follower
const ticket = await master.buyMarket('EURUSD', 0.01);
// … the copier mirrors the open (and the later close) onto the follower account

Install: npm install github:MetaRPC/NodeCopier alongside NodeMT4 (npm install github:MetaRPC/NodeMT4). Both install under their @metarpc/* package names, so the imports above work as-is.

Risk sizing (the copier's riskType): FixedLot · LotMultiplier · BalanceMultiplier · FixedBalanceMultiplier · EquityMultiplier. Plus copySl / copyTp / copyPendingOrders / reverseCopy.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & gotchas
docs.text:
• Two services, two endpoints. NodeMT4 talks to mt4.mrpc.pro; NodeCopier to copy.mrpc.pro. The copier is a companion service, not a replacement.
  • Owner key required for the copier. TRIAL works for a first look on a terminal, but the copier needs a real owner user_key.
  • Transport success ≠ broker execution. A successful start means the copier was created — confirm the follower actually opened the trade (NodeCopier's trade logs, or read the follower with NodeMT4's openedOrders).
  • MT4 is order-centric. Copied trades land as MT4 orders (one ticket per fill, no netting) — the same model NodeMT4 exposes.
  • Demo-first. Use disposable demo accounts for copier tests. Hosted terminals and running copiers are billed separately (see pricing).

docs.title: MT4Account — Master Overview
docs.text:
One page to orient fast: what lives where, how to choose the right API, and jump links to every overview and method spec in this docs set.

MT4Account (from @metarpc/nodemt4) is the low-level layer — a thin, 1:1-with-the-wire client. Each method maps to a single gRPC RPC: you pass a generated protobuf *Request and get back the reply's *Data payload, or it rejects with an MrpcError. It owns the gRPC channel, the service clients, the auth metadata (apikey + terminal id) and the connection lifecycle.

import { MT4Account } from '@metarpc/nodemt4';

When to use this layer

Use MT4Account when you need a field the friendly layers do not expose, or full control over the exact request. For everyday work prefer MT4Service (plain args + typed objects) or MT4Sugar (one-liners).

docs.title: 🔌 Usage pattern (raw gRPC)
docs.text:
Every method is called on an MT4Account. It owns the gRPC channel, sends the terminal id and API key as metadata, and unwraps the reply — returning the protobuf *Data payload or rejecting with an error.

import { MT4Account } from '@metarpc/nodemt4';

// Create the client (prepares the gRPC channel; apiKey from MRPC_API_KEY, else TRIAL)
const account = new MT4Account('mt4.mrpc.pro', 443);

// Connect the terminal (ConnectEx by broker server name)
await account.connect({ user: 500000, password: 'password', server: 'TeleTrade-Demo' });
// The gateway returns a terminal session GUID; later calls reuse it automatically.

// Call a method: returns the Data payload, or throws MrpcError / a transport error
const s = await account.accountSummary();
console.log('Balance:', s.getAccountBalance(), s.getAccountCurrency());

account.close();

Every method follows the same shape:

  • Proto Service/Method: Service.Method(Request) → Reply
  • Client call: account.method(req?) resolves with the *Data payload.
  • Reply structure: the reply carries either a data payload or an error; MT4Account returns the data and turns error into a thrown MrpcError.
  • Errors are exceptions — there are no error return values; await inside try/catch.

Timestamps: proto uses google.protobuf.Timestamp; read .getSeconds(). Every MT4 time is broker server time — the friendly MT4Service layer converts these to numbers / UTC for you.

Streaming methods: return a { unsubscribe() } handle. The SDK reads the stream and invokes your callback with each reply's raw *Data; call unsubscribe() to stop.

docs.title: Layer 1: MT4Account (Low-Level) — You are here!
docs.text: What: direct protobuf/gRPC communication with the MT4 terminal. Works with protobuf *Request / *Data objects; raw gRPC calls; complete access to every MT4 function; highest complexity. Location: src/MT4Account.ts

docs.title: Layer 2: MT4Service
docs.text: What: a friendly facade over MT4Account — plain arguments and typed objects (AccountInfo, Quote, OrderInfo, Bar…). No protobuf. Location: src/MT4Service.ts → overview.

docs.title: Layer 3: MT4Sugar
docs.text:
What: high-level convenience API — one-liners, risk-based position sizing, smart defaults. Location: src/MT4Sugar.ts → overview.

Each layer owns the one below it: MT4Sugar owns an MT4Service, which owns an MT4Account. From Sugar you can always reach down with sugar.service() and sugar.account().

docs.title: 💡 Key concepts
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions. A server-side rejection throws MrpcError (carrying mqlIntCode / mqlDescription); a transport failure throws the gRPC error. There are no error return values.
  • Session id is automatic. connect() (ConnectEx) obtains a terminal session GUID; the SDK attaches it (+ your apikey) to every later call and stream. You never call GetId manually.
  • MT4 is order-centric. Unlike MT5, MT4 has no positions and no netting — every fill is an order with a ticket, identified by an OrderSendOperationType (OP_BUY, OP_SELL, OP_BUYLIMIT, …). "Positions" in the friendly layers simply means the open market orders (types BUY/SELL).
  • Trade outcome. MT4 reports the broker's verdict as an MQL error number (mqlIntCode: 130 invalid stops, 131 invalid volume, 132 market closed, 134 not enough money, 138 requote, 128 trade timeout). A trade whose transport fails after the request may have reached the terminal becomes a TradeOutcomeUnknownError and is never re-sent.
  • Everything is server time. MT4 has no per-message UTC; use serverTimezone() or accountSummary().getUtcServerTimeShiftMinutes() to convert.

"Trade safe, code clean, and may your gRPC streams always flow smoothly."

docs.title: ✅ Getting an Account Summary
docs.text:
Request: full account summary (AccountSummaryData) from MT4. Fetch all core account metrics in a single call.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.accountSummary(...) (from @metarpc/nodemt4)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Proto definition: AccountSummary (defined in mt4-term-api-account-helper.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Method: AccountSummary(AccountSummaryRequest) → AccountSummaryReply
  • Low-level client (generated): AccountHelperClient.accountSummary(request, metadata, opts, cb)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A single RPC returning core account state: balance, equity, credit, currency, leverage, trade mode, server time.
  • Why you need it. Fast dashboard / CLI status; double-check login / currency / leverage; connection heartbeat via getServerTime().
  • Sanity check. If getAccountLogin(), getAccountCurrency(), getAccountLeverage() and getAccountEquity() are set → the connection is alive.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Use it to display real-time account state and sanity-check connectivity:

  • Dashboard / CLI status in one call.
  • Verify balance & equity before trading.
  • Terminal heartbeat via getServerTime() and getUtcServerTimeShiftMinutes().

Prefer plain values? MT4Service.getAccountInfo() returns a friendly AccountInfo object (named fields, times as numbers) instead of protobuf.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
import { MT4Account, AccountHelperPb } from '@metarpc/nodemt4';

class MT4Account {
  // Retrieves core account information in a single call.
  // Returns the raw AccountSummaryData (read fields with getXxx()); throws MrpcError on failure.
  accountSummary(req?: any /* AccountSummaryRequest */): Promise<any /* AccountSummaryData */>;
}

Request message:

AccountSummaryRequest {} (empty message — the argument is optional and defaults to an empty request)

Reply message:

AccountSummaryReply {
  oneof response {
    AccountSummaryData data = 1;
    Error error = 2;
  }
}

MT4Account unwraps the oneof: it resolves with data on success and rejects with MrpcError (carrying the server-side Error) otherwise.

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text:
Parameter Type Description req AccountSummaryRequest (optional) Empty request message. Omit it to use new AccountHelperPb.AccountSummaryRequest().

There is no ctx/timeout parameter. Each call runs on a per-call deadline from the client (callTimeoutMs, default 30000 ms — accountSummary uses 15000 ms internally). Tune it on the account:

account.callTimeoutMs = 5000;   // deadline for ordinary read RPCs

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — AccountSummaryData
docs.text:
Field (proto) JS accessor Type Description AccountLogin getAccountLogin() number Trading account login (ID). AccountBalance getAccountBalance() number Balance excluding floating P/L. AccountEquity getAccountEquity() number Equity = balance + floating P/L. AccountCredit getAccountCredit() number Credit amount. AccountUserName getAccountUserName() string Account holder name. AccountLeverage getAccountLeverage() number Leverage (e.g. 100 for 1:100). AccountCurrency getAccountCurrency() string Deposit currency (e.g. "USD"). AccountCompanyName getAccountCompanyName() string Broker / company display name. AccountTradeMode getAccountTradeMode() EnumAccountTradeMode Demo / Contest / Real — see enum below. IsInvestor getIsInvestor() boolean Connected with the read-only investor password. ServerTime getServerTime() Timestamp Server time at response (broker time zone). .getSeconds() → unix seconds. UtcServerTimeShiftMinutes getUtcServerTimeShiftMinutes() number Add this many minutes to UTC to get broker server time.

🧮 Floating profit: the summary has no dedicated profit field — compute getAccountEquity() - getAccountBalance().

docs.title: ⚠️ Margin fields on MT4
docs.text: AccountSummaryData also declares getAccountMargin(), getAccountMarginFree(), getAccountMarginLevel(), getAccountMarginMode(), getAccountTradeAllowed() and getAccountTradeExpert() (the proto is shared with MT5). On MT4 the gateway typically returns 0 / defaults for the margin fields — do not rely on them here. For live margin, read one OnOpenedOrdersProfit snapshot, or use MT4Sugar.getMargin() / getFreeMargin() / getMarginLevel(), which do exactly that.

docs.title: 🧱 Related enums (from proto)
docs.text: 💡 Enum usage note: the generated enums are namespace objects on the *Pb modules. Compare against the full constant, e.g. s.getAccountTradeMode() === AccountHelperPb.EnumAccountTradeMode.ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_DEMO.

docs.title: EnumAccountTradeMode
docs.text:
enum EnumAccountTradeMode {
  ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_DEMO    = 0;  // demo / practice
  ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_CONTEST = 1;  // contest
  ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_REAL    = 2;  // real trading
}

import { AccountHelperPb } from '@metarpc/nodemt4';
const M = AccountHelperPb.EnumAccountTradeMode;

function tradeModeToString(mode: number): string {
  switch (mode) {
    case M.ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_DEMO:    return 'DEMO';
    case M.ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_CONTEST: return 'CONTEST';
    case M.ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_REAL:    return 'REAL';
    default:                           return `UNKNOWN(${mode})`;
  }
}

docs.title: EnumAccountMarginMode
docs.text:
getAccountMarginMode() is enum-typed on the shared proto, but inert on MT4 — the gateway returns 0 (RETAIL_NETTING). It's an MT5 margin concept; MT4 is order-centric (no netting/hedging margin modes). Listed for completeness:

enum EnumAccountMarginMode {
  ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE_RETAIL_NETTING = 0;  // MT4 default (reported value)
  ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE_EXCHANGE       = 1;  // exchange margin (MT5)
  ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE_RETAIL_HEDGING = 2;  // hedging margin  (MT5)
}

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions: a server-side rejection rejects with MrpcError; a transport failure rejects with the gRPC error. await inside try/catch.
  • Default timeout: read RPCs use callTimeoutMs (default 30000 ms); accountSummary uses 15000 ms.
  • Timestamps: getServerTime() is a google.protobuf.Timestamp; read .getSeconds() for unix seconds, or use the friendly MT4Service.getAccountInfo() which returns numbers.
  • Session is automatic: connect() obtains the terminal id and the SDK attaches it to this call — you never pass it yourself.

docs.title: 1) Basic usage
docs.text:
import { MT4Account } from '@metarpc/nodemt4';

async function main() {
  const account = new MT4Account('mt4.mrpc.pro', 443);     // apiKey from MRPC_API_KEY, else TRIAL
  await account.connect({ user: 500000, password: 'password', server: 'TeleTrade-Demo' });

  const s = await account.accountSummary();
  console.log('Account Login:', s.getAccountLogin());
  console.log(`Balance: ${s.getAccountBalance().toFixed(2)} ${s.getAccountCurrency()}`);
  console.log('Equity:', s.getAccountEquity().toFixed(2));
  console.log('Leverage: 1:' + s.getAccountLeverage());

  account.close();
}
main().catch(console.error);

docs.title: 2) Compact status line for a CLI
docs.text:
async function printAccountStatus(account: MT4Account) {
  try {
    const s = await account.accountSummary();
    console.log(
      `Acc ${s.getAccountLogin()} | ${s.getAccountCurrency()} | ` +
      `Bal ${s.getAccountBalance().toFixed(2)} | Eq ${s.getAccountEquity().toFixed(2)} | ` +
      `Lev 1:${s.getAccountLeverage()} | Mode ${tradeModeToString(s.getAccountTradeMode())}`
    );
  } catch (e) {
    console.log('❌ Error:', e.message);
  }
}
// Output: Acc 500000 | USD | Bal 10000.00 | Eq 10050.25 | Lev 1:100 | Mode DEMO

docs.title: 3) Floating profit (no dedicated field)
docs.text:
async function printFloating(account: MT4Account) {
  const s = await account.accountSummary();
  const floating = s.getAccountEquity() - s.getAccountBalance();   // no dedicated profit field
  console.log('Floating P/L:', floating.toFixed(2));
}

docs.title: 4) Server time with timezone shift
docs.text:
async function printServerTime(account: MT4Account) {
  const s = await account.accountSummary();
  const broker = new Date(s.getServerTime().getSeconds() * 1000);
  const shift = s.getUtcServerTimeShiftMinutes();                 // minutes to add to UTC
  const utc = new Date(broker.getTime() - shift * 60000);
  console.log('Server time (broker):', broker.toISOString());
  console.log('Server time (UTC):   ', utc.toISOString());
  console.log('Broker offset from UTC:', shift, 'minutes');
}

docs.title: 5) Structured data model
docs.text:
interface AccountSummaryView {
  login: number; currency: string; balance: number; equity: number;
  floating: number; leverage: number; tradeMode: string; company: string;
}

function fromProto(s: any): AccountSummaryView {
  return {
    login: s.getAccountLogin(), currency: s.getAccountCurrency(),
    balance: s.getAccountBalance(), equity: s.getAccountEquity(),
    floating: s.getAccountEquity() - s.getAccountBalance(),
    leverage: s.getAccountLeverage(), tradeMode: tradeModeToString(s.getAccountTradeMode()),
    company: s.getAccountCompanyName(),
  };
}

const view = fromProto(await account.accountSummary());
console.log(view);

docs.title: 6) Error handling
docs.text:
async function tryGetSummary(account: MT4Account) {
  try {
    return await account.accountSummary();
  } catch (e) {
    console.log('Failed to get account summary:', e.message);
    return null;
  }
}

docs.title: Health check
docs.text:
async function isAccountHealthy(account: MT4Account): Promise<boolean> {
  try {
    const s = await account.accountSummary();
    return s.getAccountLogin() > 0 && s.getAccountCurrency() !== '' && s.getAccountLeverage() > 0;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

docs.title: Monitor account changes
docs.text:
function monitorAccount(account: MT4Account, intervalMs: number) {
  setInterval(async () => {
    try {
      const s = await account.accountSummary();
      console.log(`[${new Date().toISOString().slice(11, 19)}] Balance: ${s.getAccountBalance().toFixed(2)} | Equity: ${s.getAccountEquity().toFixed(2)}`);
    } catch (e) {
      console.log('❌ Error:', e.message);
    }
  }, intervalMs);
}
// Usage: monitorAccount(account, 5000);

docs.title: MT4Account · Account Information — Overview
docs.text:
Balance, equity, credit, leverage and trade mode in one call — plus aggregated trade statistics, the equity curve and unrealized-P/L extrema. Use this page to choose the right API for reading account state and performance.

These methods are read-only. accountSummary lives on mt4_term_api.AccountHelper; the statistics methods on mt4_term_api.TradeStats. Each resolves with the raw *Data (read fields with getXxx()), or rejects with MrpcError.

docs.title: 📁 What lives here
docs.text:
• AccountSummary — all account info at once (login, balance, equity, credit, leverage, currency, trade mode, server time). Returns the EnumAccountTradeMode enum.
  • TradeStats — aggregated statistics over a window: trades, profit factor, expectancy, best/worst, drawdowns, Sharpe, Z-score, …
  • TradeStatsEquityHistory — the same stats plus the equity curve and the trades behind it.
  • EquityHistory — just the equity-curve points (balance / equity / drawdown per point).
  • TradeUnrealizedPL — the best/worst unrealized P/L reached per open order.

docs.title: 🧭 Plain English
docs.text:
• AccountSummary → the one-stop shop for a complete snapshot. One RPC, everything you need for a dashboard, a pre-trade affordability check, or a connection heartbeat.
  • TradeStats / EquityHistory / TradeUnrealizedPL → performance analytics over a time window — win rate, profit factor, the equity curve for a chart, and how far each open order ran into profit or loss.

Rule of thumb: need the current snapshot → accountSummary; need performance over time → the TradeStats family.

docs.title: Quick choose
docs.text: If you need… Use Returns Complete account snapshot (all values) accountSummary AccountSummaryData Aggregated stats over a window tradeStats StatsData Stats and the equity curve + trades tradeStatsEquityHistory StatsWithChartsData Just the equity-curve points equityHistory EquityHistoryData Unrealized-P/L extrema per open order tradeUnrealizedPl TradeUnrealizedPLData

docs.title: ❌ Cross-refs & gotchas
docs.text:
• Margin on MT4. AccountSummaryData exposes getAccountMargin() / getAccountMarginFree() / getAccountMarginLevel(), but the MT4 gateway often returns 0 for them — the reliable source of live margin is the OnOpenedOrdersProfit stream (or the friendly MT4Sugar.getMargin(), which reads one snapshot of it).
  • Floating profit — the summary carries no dedicated profit field; compute getAccountEquity() − getAccountBalance().
  • Time windows are UTC. The TradeStats requests take a setFromUtc(Timestamp) — pass a real UTC instant; the SDK converts for you in MT4Service.getTradeStats(from).
  • Everything else is server time. getServerTime() is broker time; use getUtcServerTimeShiftMinutes() (or serverTimezone) to convert.
  • Timeouts — read RPCs use callTimeoutMs (default 30000 ms); the stats methods use a longer deadline internally.

docs.title: 🟢 Minimal snippets
docs.text:
// Complete account snapshot
const s = await account.accountSummary();
console.log(
  `Balance: ${s.getAccountBalance().toFixed(2)} ${s.getAccountCurrency()}, ` +
  `Equity: ${s.getAccountEquity().toFixed(2)}, Leverage: 1:${s.getAccountLeverage()}`,
);

// Aggregated statistics for the last 30 days
import { TradeStatsPb } from '@metarpc/nodemt4';

const req = new TradeStatsPb.TradeStatsRequest();
req.setFromUtc(new Date(Date.now() - 30 * 864e5).toISOString());   // 30 days ago, UTC
const stats = await account.tradeStats(req);
console.log(`trades ${stats.getTrades()}  profit factor ${stats.getProfitFactor().toFixed(2)}`);

// The equity curve as points
const eq = new TradeStatsPb.EquityHistoryRequest();
eq.setFromUtc(new Date(Date.now() - 30 * 864e5).toISOString());
const curve = await account.equityHistory(eq);
console.log(`equity-curve points: ${curve.getPointsList().length}`);

Prefer plain values? The friendly layer does the request-building and mapping for you: MT4Service.getAccountInfo(), getTradeStats(from), getEquityHistory(from).

docs.title: 📉 Equity History
docs.text:
Request: the account's equity-curve points (EquityHistoryData) over a window — balance, equity, realized/unrealized P/L and drawdowns per point. Perfect for an equity chart.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.equityHistory(request) (from @metarpc/nodemt4)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.TradeStats
  • Proto definition: EquityHistory (defined in mt4-term-api-trade-stats.proto)

docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.TradeStats
  • Method: EquityHistory(EquityHistoryRequest) → EquityHistoryReply
  • Low-level client (generated): TradeStatsClient.equityHistory(request, metadata, opts, cb)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Just the equity curve — a list of points, each with balance / equity / drawdown.
  • Why you need it. Draw an equity chart, or compute your own drawdown / return metrics.
  • Sanity check. getPointsList().length is the number of points; 0 means the window is empty.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Use it when you only need the curve (not the full stats of tradeStatsEquityHistory). Read-only.

Prefer plain values? MT4Service.getEquityHistory(from, excludeSameBars?) returns a typed EquityPoint[] (times as numbers).

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:

class MT4Account {
  // The equity-curve points. Returns the raw EquityHistoryData; throws MrpcError on failure.
  equityHistory(req: any /* EquityHistoryRequest */): Promise<any /* EquityHistoryData */>;
}

Request message:

EquityHistoryRequest {
  string from             = 1;  // window start, server time
  string from_utc         = 2;  // window start, UTC (prefer this)
  bool                      exclude_same_bars = 3;  // drop consecutive equal points
}

Reply message: EquityHistoryReply { oneof response { EquityHistoryData data = 1; Error error = 2; } }.

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description req EquityHistoryRequest setFromUtc(isoUtcString) — window start (UTC). setExcludeSameBars(true) drops flat points (smaller payload).

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — EquityHistoryData
docs.text:
getPointsList() → EquityPointData[]. Each point:

JS accessor Type Description getBalance() number Balance at the point. getEquity() number Equity at the point. getRealizedPl() number Realized P/L up to the point. getUnrealizedPl() number Floating P/L at the point. getCashFlow() number Deposits / withdrawals at the point. getBalanceDrawdownRaw() / ...Relative() number Balance drawdown (currency / percent). getEquityDrawdownRaw() / ...Relative() number Equity drawdown (currency / percent). getTime() Timestamp Point time, broker server time (.getSeconds()). getTimeUtc() Timestamp The same moment in UTC.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• UTC window: set from_utc. Points carry both getTime() (server) and getTimeUtc() (UTC).
  • Thin the curve with setExcludeSameBars(true) for long windows.
  • Errors are exceptions: rejects with MrpcError / the gRPC error.

docs.title: 1) Fetch and print the last points
docs.text:
import { MT4Account, TradeStatsPb, toTimestamp } from '@metarpc/nodemt4';

const req = new TradeStatsPb.EquityHistoryRequest();
req.setFromUtc(new Date(Date.now() - 7 * 864e5).toISOString());   // last 7 days
req.setExcludeSameBars(true);

const d = await account.equityHistory(req);
for (const p of d.getPointsList().slice(-5)) {
  const t = new Date(p.getTimeUtc().getSeconds() * 1000).toISOString().slice(0, 16);
  console.log(`${t}  equity ${p.getEquity().toFixed(2)}  bal ${p.getBalance().toFixed(2)}`);

docs.title: 2) Max drawdown from the curve
docs.text:
let peak = -Infinity, maxDD = 0;
for (const p of d.getPointsList()) {
  peak = Math.max(peak, p.getEquity());
  maxDD = Math.max(maxDD, peak - p.getEquity());
}
console.log('max equity drawdown:', maxDD.toFixed(2));

docs.text: const series = d.getPointsList().map((p: any) => [p.getTimeUtc().getSeconds() * 1000, p.getEquity()]);

docs.title: 📊 Trade Statistics
docs.text:
Request: aggregated trading statistics (StatsData) over a time window — win rate, profit factor, expectancy, drawdowns, best/worst, Sharpe, Z-score and more.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.tradeStats(request) (from @metarpc/nodemt4)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.TradeStats
  • Proto definition: TradeStats (defined in mt4-term-api-trade-stats.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt4_term_api.TradeStats
  • Method: TradeStats(TradeStatsRequest) → TradeStatsReply
  • Low-level client (generated): TradeStatsClient.tradeStats(request, metadata, opts, cb)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One RPC that scans the account's closed trades since a start time and returns a full performance report.
  • Why you need it. Dashboards, strategy scorecards, risk reviews — profit factor, expectancy, drawdowns and win counts without computing them yourself.
  • Sanity check. If getTrades() is 0, the window has no closed trades — widen from.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Use it to score performance over any window: today, this week, since inception. It is read-only and does not touch open orders.

Prefer plain values? MT4Service.getTradeStats(from) builds the request and returns a typed TradeStats object.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
import { MT4Account, TradeStatsPb, toTimestamp } from '@metarpc/nodemt4';

class MT4Account {
  // Aggregated statistics over a window. Returns the raw StatsData; throws MrpcError on failure.
  tradeStats(req: any /* TradeStatsRequest */): Promise<any /* StatsData */>;
}

Request message:

TradeStatsRequest {
  string from     = 1;  // window start, broker server time
  string from_utc = 2;  // window start, UTC  (prefer this)
}

Reply message: TradeStatsReply { oneof response { StatsData data = 1; Error error = 2; } } — MT4Account resolves with data or rejects with MrpcError.

docs.title: 🔽 Input
⬆️ Output — StatsData
docs.text:
JS accessor Type Description getTrades() number Number of closed trades in the window. getProfitability() number Net profit (deposit currency). getProfitFactor() number Gross profit ÷ gross loss (>1 is profitable). getExpectancy() number Average result per trade. getGrowthPercent() number Account growth over the window, percent. getGhpr() number Geometric holding-period return. getSharpeRatio() number Risk-adjusted return. getZScore() number Streak (win/loss clustering) measure. getStandardDeviation() number Dispersion of trade results. getPips() number Net pips. getLots() number Total volume traded (lots). getDeposits() / getWithdrawals() number Cash movements in the window. getComissions() number Total commissions (sic — proto spelling). getBestTrade() / getWorstTrade() number Largest win / loss (currency). getBestTradePips() / getWorstTradePips() number Largest win / loss (pips). getAverageWin() / getAverageLost() number Mean win / mean loss. getAverageTradeLength() number Mean holding time. getLongsWon() / getShortsWon() number Winning long / short trades. getMaxBalanceDrawdownRaw() / ...Relative() number Max balance drawdown (currency / percent). getMaxEquityDrawdownRaw() / ...Relative() number Max equity drawdown (currency / percent). getMarketsList() string[] Symbols traded in the window.

Timestamps are UTC: always set from_utc; leaving both unset returns stats over the whole history the gateway keeps.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions: rejects with MrpcError on a server error, or the gRPC error on transport failure.
  • Heavier than a read: this call scans history — the SDK uses the default callTimeoutMs.
  • Empty window: no closed trades → getTrades() === 0 and the ratios are 0.

docs.title: 1) Last 30 days
docs.text:
import { MT4Account, TradeStatsPb, toTimestamp } from '@metarpc/nodemt4';

const account = new MT4Account('mt4.mrpc.pro', 443);
await account.connect({ user: 500000, password: 'password', server: 'TeleTrade-Demo' });

const req = new TradeStatsPb.TradeStatsRequest();
req.setFromUtc(new Date(Date.now() - 30 * 864e5).toISOString());
const s = await account.tradeStats(req);

console.log(`trades ${s.getTrades()}  profit ${s.getProfitability().toFixed(2)}`);
console.log(`profit factor ${s.getProfitFactor().toFixed(2)}  expectancy ${s.getExpectancy().toFixed(2)}`);
console.log(`best ${s.getBestTrade().toFixed(2)}  worst ${s.getWorstTrade().toFixed(2)}`);

docs.title: 2) A compact scorecard
docs.text:
function scorecard(s: any): string {
  return `PF ${s.getProfitFactor().toFixed(2)} | ` +
    `win ${s.getLongsWon() + s.getShortsWon()}/${s.getTrades()} | ` +
    `DD ${s.getMaxEquityDrawdownRelative().toFixed(1)}% | ` +
    `growth ${s.getGrowthPercent().toFixed(1)}%`;
}

docs.title: 3) Since the start of the year
docs.text:
const jan1 = new Date(Date.UTC(new Date().getUTCFullYear(), 0, 1));
const req = new TradeStatsPb.TradeStatsRequest();
req.setFromUtc(jan1.toISOString());
const s = await account.tradeStats(req);
console.log('YTD profit:', s.getProfitability().toFixed(2), 'over', s.getTrades(), 'trades');

docs.text:
Request: the aggregated statistics and the equity curve and the trades behind them (StatsWithChartsData) in one call — everything you need to render a performance page.

API Information:

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A superset of tradeStats: the StatsData plus the equity-curve points and the trade lists.
  • Why you need it. One round-trip to draw a full report page — headline stats + an equity chart + a trade table.
  • Sanity check. getStats().getTrades() mirrors tradeStats; getChartsList() holds the curve.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Use it when you want the numbers and the chart data together. It is read-only.

Prefer plain values? MT4Service.getTradeStatsEquityHistory(from, excludeSameBars?) returns { stats, equity } with a typed TradeStats and EquityPoint[].

docs.text:

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — StatsWithChartsData

• Heavier call — it returns both the report and the full curve; keep the window reasonable or set excludeSameBars.
  • Errors are exceptions: rejects with MrpcError / the gRPC error.
  • UTC window: set from_utc.

docs.title: 1) Stats headline + curve length
