  • OpenedOrders — the current book on demand.
  • Friendly layer: MT4Service.subscribeTrades(cb).

docs.title: MT4Account · Streaming Methods — Overview
docs.text:
Real-time server streams: live ticks, trade events, periodic order-profit snapshots (with margin!), ticket snapshots, and terminal connection state. Each returns a { unsubscribe() } handle.

These methods live on mt4_term_api.SubscriptionService (and Connection for onConnectState). Each takes a protobuf *Request and a callback that receives every reply's raw *Data; errors (and an unexpected end) go to onError. Mapping to typed objects happens one layer up, in MT4Service.

docs.title: 📁 What lives here
docs.text:
• OnSymbolTick — live ticks for one or more symbols.
  • OnTrade — trade events: fills, modifications, closes (new / updated / removed / history orders).
  • OnOpenedOrdersProfit — periodic snapshot of open orders with live profit + account info (including margin — which AccountSummary lacks on MT4).
  • OnOpenedOrdersTickets — periodic list of open / pending ticket numbers.
  • OnConnectState — terminal connection-state events (connected / alive).

docs.title: 🔌 The stream shape
docs.text:
const sub = account.onSymbolTick(req, (data) => {
  // data is the raw *Data of each reply — read it with getXxx()
}, (err) => {
  // error reply, transport failure, or an unexpected end
});

// later:
sub.unsubscribe();   // stops the stream (a cancel is NOT reported as an error)
  • The callback fires once per reply with the raw payload.
  • onError fires on an error reply, a transport failure, or if the stream ends unexpectedly. Re-subscribe after a transport error.
  • unsubscribe() cancels cleanly — it is not surfaced to onError.

docs.title: Quick choose
docs.text: If you need… Use Payload (raw *Data) Live prices onSymbolTick getSymbolTick() (bid/ask/last/volume/time) Fills / modifications / closes onTrade getType(), getEventData(), getAccountInfo() Live profit + margin, on a timer onOpenedOrdersProfit getOpenedOrdersWithProfitUpdatedList(), getAccountInfo() Open/pending tickets, on a timer onOpenedOrdersTickets getPositionTicketsList(), getPendingOrderTicketsList() Terminal connection health onConnectState getIsConnected(), getIsAlive(), getState()

docs.title: ❌ Gotchas
docs.text:
• Select symbols first. onSymbolTick only streams symbols that are in Market Watch — SymbolSelect them.
  • Live margin lives here. MT4's AccountSummary margin fields are often 0; read OnOpenedOrdersProfit's getAccountInfo() (or MT4Sugar.getMargin()).
  • Handle reconnects. On a transport error, onError fires — re-subscribe (and reconnect() the account if the terminal was lost).
  • Always unsubscribe when done to free the stream.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Friendly streams: MT4Service.subscribeQuotes/subscribeTrades/subscribeOpenedOrdersProfit/subscribeOpenedOrdersTickets/subscribeConnectState — the same streams, mapped to typed objects.

Back to: MT4Account — Master Overview

docs.title: MT4Service — Account Methods (Mid-Level API)
docs.text:
Connect, then read account state and performance as plain typed objects — no protobuf, no getXxx() chains.

🧩 API Layer: MID-LEVEL — a friendly facade over MT4Account that returns plain JS types and typed objects.

Implementation: src/MT4Service.ts, wrapping the low-level accountSummary and TradeStats calls on MT4Account.

Demos: examples/demos/service/04_service_demo.js · examples/demos/run_all.js.

← MT4Service Overview · low-level group ↓

docs.title: 🎯 Why these methods exist
docs.text:
Problem — on MT4Account, accountSummary() returns a protobuf *Data you must unwrap, and the stats calls need you to build a TradeStatsRequest and set a UTC timestamp yourself:

// Low-level (MT4Account)
import { TradeStatsPb, toTimestamp } from '@metarpc/nodemt4';
const req = new TradeStatsPb.TradeStatsRequest();
req.setFromUtc(new Date(Date.now() - 30 * 864e5).toISOString());
const s = await account.tradeStats(req);
console.log(s.getProfitFactor());   // .getXxx() everywhere

Solution — MT4Service builds the requests and maps the replies to typed objects:

// Mid-level (MT4Service)
const a = await service.getAccountInfo();                 // AccountInfo
const stats = await service.getTradeStats(new Date(Date.now() - 30 * 864e5)); // TradeStats
console.log(a.balance, stats.profitFactor);               // ✅ plain fields

Advantages

  • ✅ One call → the whole account as a typed AccountInfo.
  • ✅ Plain JS types — no .getXxx(), no enum imports.
  • ✅ tradeMode decoded to 'DEMO' | 'CONTEST' | 'REAL'.
  • ✅ The stats methods take a plain Date and handle the UTC request for you.

docs.title: 🔌 Connection lifecycle
📋 Account methods
docs.text: Method Returns Low-level equivalent getAccountInfo() Promise<AccountInfo> accountSummary(), mapped getTradeStats(from) Promise<TradeStats> tradeStats(req) getTradeStatsEquityHistory(from, excludeSameBars?) Promise<{ stats, equity }> tradeStatsEquityHistory(req) getEquityHistory(from, excludeSameBars?) Promise<EquityPoint[]> equityHistory(req) getTradeUnrealizedPl(from) Promise<any[]> tradeUnrealizedPl(req)

docs.title: 📦 AccountInfo (DTO)
docs.text:
Returned by getAccountInfo():

Field Type Description login number Account number. currency string Deposit currency. balance number Balance (without floating P/L). equity number Equity (balance + floating P/L). credit number Credit. leverage number Leverage (100 = 1:100). name string Account holder. company string Broker name. server string Trade server (e.g. TeleTrade-Demo). tradeMode 'DEMO' \| 'CONTEST' \| 'REAL' \| 'UNKNOWN' Decoded account type. tradeModeCode number Raw trade-mode enum value. isInvestor boolean Connected with the investor (read-only) password. serverTime number Broker server time — seconds since epoch. utcServerShiftMinutes number serverTime = utc + shift·60 — use it to build server-time windows.

⚠️ No margin here. MT4's AccountSummary carries no reliable margin — AccountInfo omits it. For live margin / free margin / margin level use MT4Sugar.getMargin() (or the subscribeOpenedOrdersProfit stream), which read an OnOpenedOrdersProfit snapshot. Floating profit = equity − balance.

docs.title: 📈 TradeStats & EquityPoint (DTOs)
docs.text:
getTradeStats(from) → TradeStats: trades, profitability, profitFactor, expectancy, ghpr, growthPercent, sharpeRatio, zScore, standardDeviation, pips, lots, deposits, withdrawals, commissions, bestTrade, worstTrade, bestTradePips, worstTradePips, averageWin, averageLost, averageTradeLength, longsWon, shortsWon, maxBalanceDrawdownRaw/Relative, maxEquityDrawdownRaw/Relative, markets.

getEquityHistory(from) → EquityPoint[]: each { time, timeUtc, balance, equity, realizedPl, unrealizedPl, cashFlow, balanceDrawdownRaw/Relative, equityDrawdownRaw/Relative }.

docs.title: 1) getAccountInfo(): Promise<AccountInfo>
docs.text:
The whole account in one call.

const a = await service.getAccountInfo();
console.log(`${a.name} #${a.login} on ${a.server}`);
console.log(`balance ${a.balance.toFixed(2)} ${a.currency}  equity ${a.equity.toFixed(2)}  1:${a.leverage}  ${a.tradeMode}`);
console.log('floating P/L:', (a.equity - a.balance).toFixed(2));

docs.title: 2) getTradeStats(from: Date | number): Promise<TradeStats>
docs.text:
Aggregated statistics since from (UTC).

const s = await service.getTradeStats(new Date(Date.now() - 30 * 864e5));   // last 30 days
console.log(`trades ${s.trades}  PF ${s.profitFactor.toFixed(2)}  growth ${s.growthPercent.toFixed(1)}%`);
console.log(`best ${s.bestTrade.toFixed(2)}  worst ${s.worstTrade.toFixed(2)}  maxDD ${s.maxEquityDrawdownRelative.toFixed(1)}%`);

docs.title: 3) getEquityHistory(from, excludeSameBars = false): Promise<EquityPoint[]>
docs.text:
The equity-curve points for a chart.

const curve = await service.getEquityHistory(new Date(Date.now() - 7 * 864e5), true);
const series = curve.map((p) => [p.timeUtc, p.equity]);   // ready for a chart
console.log('points:', curve.length);

docs.title: 4) getTradeStatsEquityHistory(from, excludeSameBars = false): Promise<{ stats, equity }>
docs.text:
Stats and the curve in one call.

const { stats, equity } = await service.getTradeStatsEquityHistory(new Date(Date.now() - 90 * 864e5));
console.log(`PF ${stats.profitFactor.toFixed(2)} over ${stats.trades} trades, ${equity.length} curve points`);

docs.title: 5) getTradeUnrealizedPl(from: Date | number): Promise<any[]>
docs.text:
Best/worst unrealized P/L per open order since from (run-up / drawdown).

for (const e of await service.getTradeUnrealizedPl(new Date(Date.now() - 864e5))) {
  console.log(`#${e.ticket} ${e.symbol}  best +${e.maxUnrealizedPl?.toFixed?.(2)}  worst ${e.minUnrealizedPl?.toFixed?.(2)}`);
}

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions — a server error rejects with MrpcError; await inside try/catch.
  • Time windows are UTC for the stats methods (they build the UTC request for you). Account/history windows elsewhere use server time.
  • Session is automatic — connect() captures the terminal id; later calls attach it for you.

docs.title: MT4Service — Orders & History Methods (Mid-Level API)
docs.text:
Read open orders, pending orders and closed-order history as typed OrderInfo objects — the protobuf unwrapping and type filtering are done for you.

🧩 API Layer: MID-LEVEL — a friendly facade over MT4Account.

Implementation: src/MT4Service.ts. Demos: examples/demos/service/04_service_demo.js.

← MT4Service Overview · low-level group ↓

docs.title: 🎯 Why these methods exist
docs.text:
On MT4Account, openedOrders() returns a protobuf *Data whose list you iterate with getOrderInfosList() and read each order with getXxx(). MT4Service maps every order to a plain OrderInfo and adds the common filters (positions vs pending) you'd otherwise write yourself.

// Mid-level
const positions = await service.positions();           // open market orders → OrderInfo[]
const pending   = await service.pendingOrders();        // pending orders → OrderInfo[]
const { totalCount, orders } = await service.ordersHistory(from, to);

MT4 is order-centric. There are no positions in the MT5 sense — a "position" here is just an open market order (type 0 BUY / 1 SELL). Pending orders are types 2–5.

docs.title: 📋 Methods
docs.text:
Method Returns Notes openedOrders(sortType?) Promise<OrderInfo[]> All open market + pending orders. positions(magic?) Promise<OrderInfo[]> Open market orders (types 0/1), optionally filtered by magic. pendingOrders(magic?) Promise<OrderInfo[]> Pending orders (types 2–5), optionally filtered by magic. openedOrdersTickets() Promise<number[]> Just the ticket numbers. ordersHistory(from, to, opts?) Promise<OrdersHistory> Closed orders in a window (plain Dates).

opts for ordersHistory: { sort?: number; page?: number; perPage?: number } (sort defaults to close-time-desc).

docs.title: 📦 OrderInfo & OrdersHistory (DTOs)
docs.text:
OrderInfo

Field Type Description ticket number Order ticket. symbol string Symbol. type number 0 BUY · 1 SELL · 2 BUY_LIMIT · 3 SELL_LIMIT · 4 BUY_STOP · 5 SELL_STOP. lots number Volume. openPrice number Entry price. openTime number Open time, seconds (server). stopLoss / takeProfit number SL / TP (0 = none). profit number Floating P/L (open) or realized (history). swap / commission number Swap / commission. comment string Comment. magic number Magic number. expiration number Pending expiry, seconds. accountLogin number Owning account. closeTime? / closePrice? number Set for closed (history) orders.

docs.title: 1) openedOrders(sortType?): Promise<OrderInfo[]>
docs.text:
for (const o of await service.openedOrders()) {
  console.log(`#${o.ticket} ${o.symbol} type ${o.type} lots ${o.lots} P/L ${o.profit.toFixed(2)}`);
}

docs.title: 2) positions(magic?) / pendingOrders(magic?)
docs.text:
const market  = await service.positions();        // types 0/1
const pending = await service.pendingOrders();     // types 2-5
const eaOnly  = await service.positions(12345);    // only magic 12345
console.log(`${market.length} open, ${pending.length} pending`);

docs.title: 3) openedOrdersTickets(): Promise<number[]>
docs.text:
const tickets = await service.openedOrdersTickets();
console.log('open tickets:', tickets);

docs.title: 4) ordersHistory(from, to, opts?): Promise<OrdersHistory>
docs.text:
Pass plain Dates (UTC) — the facade converts to the broker's server-time window.

const { totalCount, orders } = await service.ordersHistory(
  new Date(Date.now() - 7 * 864e5),   // from
  new Date(),                          // to
  { perPage: 100, page: 0 },
);
console.log(`${totalCount} closed`);
const net = orders.reduce((s, o) => s + o.profit + o.swap + o.commission, 0);
console.log('net P/L:', net.toFixed(2));

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Floating P/L of open orders: (await service.positions()).reduce((s, o) => s + o.profit, 0) — or MT4Sugar.getTotalProfit().
  • History window is passed as Dates; internally it becomes a server-time range.
  • Errors are exceptions — await inside try/catch.

docs.title: MT4Service — Symbols & Quotes Methods (Mid-Level API)
docs.text:
Prices, contract specs, OHLC bars and the server timezone — as typed Quote / SymbolParams / Bar objects, with the request-building done for you.

🧩 API Layer: MID-LEVEL — a friendly facade over MT4Account.

Implementation: src/MT4Service.ts. Demos: examples/demos/service/04_service_demo.js.

← MT4Service Overview · low-level group ↓

docs.title: 🎯 Why these methods exist
docs.text:
On MT4Account you build a QuoteRequest / SymbolParamsManyRequest / QuoteHistoryRequest and read the reply with getXxx(). MT4Service takes plain strings and returns typed objects — and adds the conveniences the flat client had: ensureSymbol (select + wait for a quote) and lastBars (the newest N bars without computing a server-time window).

const q  = await service.quote('EURUSD');            // Quote { bid, ask, time }
const sp = await service.symbolParams('EURUSD');     // SymbolParams { digits, point, volumeMin, … }
const bars = await service.lastBars('EURUSD', 'H1', 100);  // Bar[]

docs.title: 📋 Methods
docs.text:
Method Returns Notes symbolList() Promise<{name,index}[]> Every symbol the broker exposes. symbolSelect(symbol, select?) Promise<boolean> Add/remove in Market Watch. quote(symbol) Promise<Quote> Latest bid/ask of one symbol. quoteMany(symbols) Promise<Quote[]> Latest ticks of several symbols. symbolParams(symbol) Promise<SymbolParams> Contract spec of one symbol. symbolParamsAll() Promise<SymbolParams[]> Contract spec of all symbols. tickValueWithSize(symbols) Promise<{symbol,tickValue,tickSize,contractSize}[]> Sizing inputs. getServerTimezone() Promise<ServerTimezone> Broker UTC offset. ensureSymbol(symbol, waitMs?) Promise<Quote> Select, then wait for a two-sided quote. quoteHistory(symbol, timeframe, from, to) Promise<Bar[]> OHLC bars for a window (plain Dates). lastBars(symbol, timeframe, count, shiftMin?) Promise<Bar[]> The newest count bars (window auto-widened).

Timeframe: 'M1' \| 'M5' \| 'M15' \| 'M30' \| 'H1' \| 'H4' \| 'D1' \| 'W1' \| 'MN1' or the TIMEFRAMES ordinal.

docs.title: 📦 DTOs
docs.text: Quote = { symbol, bid, ask, high, low, time } (time = seconds, server). SymbolParams = { name, description, digits, point, spreadFloat, contractSize, volumeMin, volumeMax, volumeStep, volumeLimit, stopsLevel, freezeLevel, tickValue, tickSize, swapLong, swapShort, swapMode, currencyBase, currencyProfit, currencyMargin, tradeMode, tradeExeMode, tradeCalcMode, marginInitial, marginMaintenance, isSelected, visible, bid, time, path } (the bid field is a stale snapshot — price from quote()). Bar = { time, open, high, low, close, tickVolume, realVolume, spread } (time = seconds, server; sorted ascending). ServerTimezone = { server, source, utcOffsetSeconds, utcOffsetMinutes, validatedUtc }.

docs.title: 1) quote(symbol) / quoteMany(symbols)
docs.text:
const q = await service.quote('EURUSD');
console.log(`bid ${q.bid} ask ${q.ask} spread ${(q.ask - q.bid).toFixed(5)}`);

const many = await service.quoteMany(['EURUSD', 'GBPUSD', 'USDJPY']);
for (const m of many) console.log(m.symbol, m.bid, m.ask);

docs.title: 2) symbolParams(symbol) / symbolParamsAll()
docs.text:
const sp = await service.symbolParams('EURUSD');
const pip = sp.point * (sp.digits === 3 || sp.digits === 5 ? 10 : 1);
console.log(`digits ${sp.digits}  pip ${pip}  minLot ${sp.volumeMin}  step ${sp.volumeStep}`);

docs.title: 3) ensureSymbol(symbol, waitMs = 10000)
docs.text:
Select a symbol and wait until it reports a real two-sided quote (fresh symbols show 0 for a moment).

const q = await service.ensureSymbol('BTCUSD');
console.log('ready:', q.bid, q.ask);

docs.title: 4) quoteHistory(symbol, tf, from, to) / lastBars(symbol, tf, count, shiftMin?)
docs.text:
// Newest 100 H1 bars — no server-time math needed
const info = await service.getAccountInfo();
const bars = await service.lastBars('EURUSD', 'H1', 100, info.utcServerShiftMinutes);
console.log('bars:', bars.length, 'last close', bars.at(-1)?.close);

// Or an explicit window (plain Dates)
const range = await service.quoteHistory('EURUSD', 'H1', new Date(Date.now() - 864e5), new Date());

docs.title: 5) getServerTimezone(): Promise<ServerTimezone>
docs.text:
const tz = await service.getServerTimezone();
console.log(`${tz.server}  UTC offset ${(tz.utcOffsetMinutes / 60).toFixed(1)} h`);

docs.title: 6) tickValueWithSize(symbols)
docs.text:
for (const i of await service.tickValueWithSize(['EURUSD', 'XAUUSD'])) {
  console.log(`${i.symbol}  tickValue ${i.tickValue}  tickSize ${i.tickSize}  contract ${i.contractSize}`);
}

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Select before you stream/quote — a fresh symbol reports bid=ask=0; ensureSymbol handles the wait.
  • SymbolParams.bid is stale — always price from quote() / the tick stream.
  • lastBars is the easy path for "the newest N bars"; quoteHistory is for an explicit range.
  • Errors are exceptions — await inside try/catch.

docs.title: MT4Service — Trading Methods (Mid-Level API)
docs.text:
Send, modify and close orders with plain argument objects — the facade builds the protobuf request, fills the market price from a quote, and routes through the exactly-once tradeCall.

🧩 API Layer: MID-LEVEL — a friendly facade over MT4Account.

Implementation: src/MT4Service.ts. Demos: examples/demos/service/04_service_demo.js.

← MT4Service Overview · low-level group ↓

docs.title: 🎯 Why these methods exist
docs.text:
On MT4Account you build an OrderSendRequest, look up the current price, set each field, and read the reply with getXxx(). MT4Service takes one OrderRequest object, fills the market price from quote() when you omit it, maps the result to a typed OrderResult, and still guarantees the trade is sent exactly once.

const res = await service.orderSend({ symbol: 'EURUSD', cmd: 'BUY', lots: 0.01 });  // price auto-filled
console.log('ticket', res.ticket, 'at', res.price);

docs.title: ⚠️ Exactly-once & unknown outcomes
docs.text:
Every trade routes through the SDK's tradeCall — sent once, never re-sent:

  • Broker refusal → MrpcError with mqlIntCode (130 invalid stops, 131 invalid volume, 132 market closed, 134 no money, 138 requote). err.operation names the call.
  • Unknown outcome (transport failure after the request may have landed, or MT4 128 timeout) → TradeOutcomeUnknownError. Reconcile with openedOrders() before retrying. See Return Codes.

docs.title: 📋 Methods
docs.text: Method Returns Notes orderSend(req) Promise<OrderResult> Market or pending order; market price auto-filled from quote(). orderModify(req) Promise<{ modified: boolean }> Change SL/TP (and pending price/expiration). orderClose(req) Promise<OrderCloseResult> Close a market order (full/partial) or delete a pending one; price/volume looked up when omitted. orderCloseBy(ticket, oppositeTicket) Promise<{ closePrice, profit, closeTime }> Close an order by an opposite one.

docs.title: 📦 DTOs
docs.text:
OrderRequest (input to orderSend):

Field Type Description symbol string Symbol (required). cmd / action 'BUY'\|'SELL'\|'BUY_LIMIT'\|'SELL_LIMIT'\|'BUY_STOP'\|'SELL_STOP' or number Order command (required). lots / volume number Volume (required). price number Omit for market orders → filled from quote() (ask for buys, bid for sells). slippage number Points. stopLoss / takeProfit number SL / TP prices. comment string Comment. magicNumber / magic number EA magic. expiration Date \| number Pending expiry.

OrderResult = { ticket, errorCode, price, lots, volume, comment, openTime }. OrderModifyRequest = { ticket, stopLoss?, takeProfit?, price?, expiration? }. OrderCloseRequest = { ticket, volume?/lots?, price?, slippage?, symbol?, type? }. OrderCloseResult = { mode, historyComment } (mode: 0 market closed · 1 pending deleted).

docs.title: 1) orderSend(req): Promise<OrderResult>
docs.text:
// Market BUY — price filled from the current ask
const res = await service.orderSend({ symbol: 'EURUSD', cmd: 'BUY', lots: 0.01, slippage: 30, comment: 'NodeMT4' });

// Pending BUY LIMIT with SL/TP
await service.orderSend({ symbol: 'EURUSD', cmd: 'BUY_LIMIT', lots: 0.01, price: 1.0500, stopLoss: 1.0450, takeProfit: 1.0600 });

docs.title: 2) orderModify(req): Promise<{ modified }>
docs.text:
Pass the full new SL/TP.

const r = await service.orderModify({ ticket: 123456, stopLoss: 1.0950, takeProfit: 1.1100 });
console.log('modified:', r.modified);

docs.title: 3) orderClose(req): Promise<OrderCloseResult>
docs.text:
Omit price/volume/symbol/type and the facade looks them up (one openedOrders() + quote() round-trip).

// Close the whole order
await service.orderClose({ ticket: 123456 });
// Partial close
await service.orderClose({ ticket: 123456, volume: 0.05 });

docs.title: 4) orderCloseBy(ticket, oppositeTicket)
docs.text:
const r = await service.orderCloseBy(123456, 123457);   // same symbol, opposite direction
console.log(`closed by @ ${r.closePrice}  profit ${r.profit.toFixed(2)}`);

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
import { TradeOutcomeUnknownError, MrpcError } from '@metarpc/nodemt4';
try {
  await service.orderSend({ symbol: 'EURUSD', cmd: 'BUY', lots: 0.01 });
} catch (e) {
  if (e instanceof TradeOutcomeUnknownError) { /* reconcile with openedOrders() — do NOT resend */ }
  else if (e instanceof MrpcError) console.log('refused:', e.code, e.mqlIntCode);
}

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Market price is optional — omit price for BUY/SELL and the facade fills it from quote().
  • Slippage is in points.
  • Never blind-retry a trade — on TradeOutcomeUnknownError, check openedOrders() first.
  • Errors are exceptions — await inside try/catch.

docs.title: MT4Service — Streaming Methods (Mid-Level API)
docs.text:
The same server streams as MT4Account, but mapped to typed objects — a friendly Tick, typed trade events, a live account snapshot with margin. Each returns a { unsubscribe() } handle.

🧩 API Layer: MID-LEVEL — a friendly facade over MT4Account's raw streams.

Implementation: src/MT4Service.ts. Demos: examples/demos/service/05_service_streaming.js.

← MT4Service Overview · low-level group ↓

docs.title: 🎯 Why these methods exist
docs.text:
On MT4Account, each stream delivers the raw *Data and you read it with getXxx(). MT4Service maps each payload to a plain object — subscribeQuotes gives you a Tick, subscribeTrades typed event lists, subscribeOpenedOrdersProfit a live account snapshot (including margin, which AccountSummary lacks on MT4).

const sub = service.subscribeQuotes(['EURUSD'], (tick) => {
  console.log(tick.symbol, tick.bid, tick.ask);   // ✅ plain fields
}, (err) => console.log(err.message));
// later: sub.unsubscribe();

docs.title: 📋 Methods
docs.text:
Method Callback receives Notes subscribeQuotes(symbols, cb, onError?) Tick Live ticks for the given symbols. subscribeTrades(cb, onError?) { type, newOrders, updatedOrders, removedOrders, newHistoryOrders, account } Fills / modifications / closes. subscribeOpenedOrdersProfit(intervalMs, cb, onError?) { orders, account } Periodic open-orders-with-profit + account (margin). subscribeOpenedOrdersTickets(intervalMs, cb, onError?) { positionTickets, pendingTickets, serverTime } Periodic ticket snapshot. subscribeConnectState(cb, onError?) the connection-state object Terminal connection health.

Each returns a Subscription = { unsubscribe(): void }.

docs.title: 📦 Tick (DTO)
docs.text:
Delivered by subscribeQuotes:

Field Type Description symbol string Symbol. bid / ask / last number Prices. volume number Tick volume. time number Tick time, milliseconds (server). timeUtc number The same in real UTC (ms), when the server reports it.

The account object in the trade / profit streams carries { balance, credit, equity, margin, freeMargin, profit, marginLevel, login }.

docs.title: 1) subscribeQuotes(symbols, cb, onError?)
docs.text:
const sub = service.subscribeQuotes(['EURUSD', 'GBPUSD'], (t) => {
  console.log(`${t.symbol} bid ${t.bid} ask ${t.ask} @ ${new Date(t.time).toISOString().slice(11, 23)}`);
}, (e) => console.log('tick error:', e.message || e));

setTimeout(() => sub.unsubscribe(), 5000);

docs.title: 2) subscribeTrades(cb, onError?)
docs.text:
const sub = service.subscribeTrades((ev) => {
  for (const o of ev.newOrders)     console.log('OPEN  #', o.ticket, o.symbol);
  for (const o of ev.removedOrders) console.log('CLOSE #', o.ticket, 'P/L', o.profit.toFixed(2));
  if (ev.account) console.log('equity', ev.account.equity.toFixed(2));
}, (e) => console.log('trade error:', e.message || e));

docs.title: 3) subscribeOpenedOrdersProfit(intervalMs, cb, onError?) — live margin
docs.text:
// One snapshot is enough to read margin on MT4
const sub = service.subscribeOpenedOrdersProfit(1000, (ev) => {
  if (ev.account) console.log(`equity ${ev.account.equity.toFixed(2)} margin ${ev.account.margin.toFixed(2)} free ${ev.account.freeMargin.toFixed(2)}`);
  sub.unsubscribe();
}, (e) => console.log(e.message));

docs.title: 4) subscribeOpenedOrdersTickets(intervalMs, cb, onError?)
docs.text:
const sub = service.subscribeOpenedOrdersTickets(1000, (ev) => {
  console.log('positions:', ev.positionTickets, 'pending:', ev.pendingTickets);
}, (e) => console.log(e.message));

docs.title: 5) subscribeConnectState(cb, onError?)
docs.text:
const sub = service.subscribeConnectState((state) => {
  console.log('connected:', state.isConnected, 'alive:', state.isAlive);
}, (e) => console.log(e.message));

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Select symbols first — subscribeQuotes only streams symbols in Market Watch.
  • Live margin lives here — read subscribeOpenedOrdersProfit's account (or MT4Sugar.getMargin()), not AccountInfo.
  • Re-subscribe on onError (transport failure / unexpected end); unsubscribe() is a clean cancel, not an error.
  • Always unsubscribe when done.

docs.title: MT4Service — Overview (Mid-Level API)
docs.text:
A friendly facade over MT4Account: plain arguments in, typed objects out. No protobuf, no getXxx() — MT4Service builds the requests and maps the replies to named data-transfer objects.

🧩 API Layer: MID-LEVEL — between the raw MT4Account and the one-liner MT4Sugar.

Implementation: src/MT4Service.ts. Demos: examples/demos/service/.

import { MT4Service } from '@metarpc/nodemt4';

const svc = MT4Service.create('mt4.mrpc.pro', 443);   // builds the MT4Account underneath
await svc.connect(500000, 'password', 'TeleTrade-Demo');

const info = await svc.getAccountInfo();               // → AccountInfo (typed)
const q = await svc.quote('EURUSD');                   // → Quote { bid, ask, time }
console.log(info.balance, q.bid);

svc.account();   // ↓ drop to the raw MT4Account when you need it
  • MT4Service.create(host?, port?, apiKey?, id?) → the service with an MT4Account underneath (defaults mt4.mrpc.pro:443).
  • svc.account() → the raw MT4Account.

docs.title: 📁 Method groups — one page each
docs.text:
Each group has its own page with usage examples and explanations:

  1. Account Methods — connection lifecycle + account info & trade statistics.
  2. Orders & History Methods — open / pending orders, tickets, closed history.
  3. Symbols & Quotes Methods — prices, contract specs, OHLC bars, server timezone.
  4. Trading Methods — send / modify / close orders (exactly-once).
  5. Streaming Methods — ticks, trade events, live profit & margin.

Every method returns one of these (or an array of them); times are plain numbers (seconds/ms), order types are MT4 numbers (0 BUY, 1 SELL, 2-5 pending).

docs.title: MT4Sugar — Connection (High-Level API)
docs.text:
One-liner connect and liveness checks — the fastest way onto the terminal.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — one-liners with smart defaults over MT4Service / MT4Account.

Implementation: src/MT4Sugar.ts. Demos: examples/demos/sugar/06_sugar_basics.js.

← MT4Sugar API Overview

docs.title: 🧱 Build the stack & reach the layers below
docs.text:
import { MT4Sugar } from '@metarpc/nodemt4';

// create() builds Service → Account underneath in one call
const sugar = MT4Sugar.create('mt4.mrpc.pro', 443);

await sugar.quickConnect(500000, 'password', 'TeleTrade-Demo');
// … use it …
await sugar.service().disconnect(true);
  • MT4Sugar.create(host?, port?, apiKey?, id?) → the whole stack (defaults mt4.mrpc.pro:443).
  • sugar.service() → the MT4Service underneath · sugar.account() → the MT4Account.

docs.title: 📋 Methods
docs.text: Method Returns Purpose quickConnect(login?, password?, server?) Promise<boolean> Connect; falls back to env vars. isConnected() boolean true after a successful connect. ping() Promise<boolean> Liveness probe — terminal answers.

docs.title: quickConnect(login?, password?, server?)
docs.text:
Connects by login / password / server. Any omitted argument falls back to an env var — MT4_LOGIN, MT4_PASSWORD, MT4_SERVER — so you can keep credentials out of code. Throws MrpcError if none of the three is available.

// explicit
await sugar.quickConnect(500000, 'password', 'TeleTrade-Demo');

// from env (MT4_LOGIN / MT4_PASSWORD / MT4_SERVER)
await sugar.quickConnect();

docs.title: isConnected()
docs.text: Synchronous flag — no round-trip. true once quickConnect has succeeded.

docs.title: ping()
docs.text: A lightweight health check (CheckConnect) against the terminal; returns false instead of throwing if the terminal is down — safe to call in a loop.

docs.title: 1) Connect from environment
docs.text:
const sugar = MT4Sugar.create();
if (!(await sugar.quickConnect())) throw new Error('connect failed');
console.log('connected:', sugar.isConnected());

docs.title: 2) Reconnect guard before an action
docs.text:
if (!sugar.isConnected() || !(await sugar.ping())) {
  await sugar.quickConnect();
}

docs.title: 3) Clean shutdown (frees the trial terminal)
docs.text:
try {
  // … work …
} finally {
  await sugar.service().disconnect(true); // true = delete the terminal, free the slot
}

docs.title: 🔧 Notes
docs.text:
• Env fallback makes quickConnect() with no args the norm in scripts — set MT4_LOGIN / MT4_PASSWORD / MT4_SERVER.
  • ping() never throws — it's a boolean probe.
  • Free the terminal with disconnect(true) at the end of a one-shot run (a trial allows one terminal per IP).

docs.title: MT4Sugar — Risk Management (High-Level API)
docs.text:
Size positions by risk, cap by free margin, estimate margin, derive SL/TP from pips, and pre-flight a trade.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — over MT4Service.

Implementation: src/MT4Sugar.ts. Demos: examples/demos/sugar/10_sugar_advanced.js.

← MT4Sugar API Overview

docs.title: 📋 Methods
docs.text:
Method Returns Purpose calculatePositionSize(symbol, riskPercent, stopLossPips) Promise<number> Lots so the stop risks riskPercent% of balance. getMaxLotSize(symbol) Promise<number> Largest lot the free margin (80%) allows. calculateRequiredMargin(symbol, volume) Promise<number> Margin to open volume lots. canOpenPosition(symbol, volume) Promise<{ ok, reason }> Pre-flight: availability, volume limits, free margin. calculateSLTP(symbol, dir, entry, slPips, tpPips) Promise<{ sl, tp }> Absolute SL/TP from pip distances.

All are read-only / calculations — nothing is traded.

docs.title: 📖 Method details
docs.text:
// Lot size for 1% risk over a 20-pip stop
const lots = await sugar.calculatePositionSize('EURUSD', 1.0, 20);

// Margin & cap
console.log('margin for 0.1 lots:', (await sugar.calculateRequiredMargin('EURUSD', 0.1)).toFixed(2));
console.log('max lot:', await sugar.getMaxLotSize('EURUSD'));

// SL/TP from pips (entry 0 = current ask/bid)
const { sl, tp } = await sugar.calculateSLTP('EURUSD', 'BUY', 0, 20, 40);

// Pre-flight
const can = await sugar.canOpenPosition('EURUSD', lots);
if (!can.ok) console.log('cannot open:', can.reason);

Margin estimate on MT4: calculateRequiredMargin uses the symbol's initial margin when the broker reports it, else estimates from contractSize × ask ÷ leverage.

docs.title: 1) Risk-sized entry, end to end
docs.text:
const lots = await sugar.calculatePositionSize('EURUSD', 1.0, 20);
const can = await sugar.canOpenPosition('EURUSD', lots);
if (can.ok) {
  const { sl, tp } = await sugar.calculateSLTP('EURUSD', 'BUY', 0, 20, 40);
  await sugar.buyMarketWithSLTP('EURUSD', lots, sl, tp);
}

docs.title: 🔧 Notes
docs.text:
• Free margin is read live (getFreeMargin → OnOpenedOrdersProfit); getMaxLotSize and canOpenPosition use it.
  • Pip sizing uses the spec's tickValue / tickSize; calculatePositionSize rounds to the volume step.

docs.title: MT4Sugar — Trading Helpers (High-Level API)
docs.text:
Market orders with SL/TP given as pip distances from entry — the common case in one line.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — over MT4Service.

Implementation: src/MT4Sugar.ts. Demos: examples/demos/sugar/07_sugar_trading.js.

← MT4Sugar API Overview

docs.title: 📋 Methods
docs.text:
Method Returns Purpose buyMarketWithPips(symbol, volume, stopLossPips, takeProfitPips) Promise<number> Market BUY, SL/TP as pip distances. sellMarketWithPips(symbol, volume, stopLossPips, takeProfitPips) Promise<number> Market SELL, SL/TP as pip distances.

These compute the absolute SL/TP from the current price (via calculateSLTP) and open with buyMarketWithSLTP / sellMarketWithSLTP. Returns the ticket.

docs.title: 📖 Method details
docs.text:
// BUY 0.01 lots with a 20-pip stop and 40-pip target
const ticket = await sugar.buyMarketWithPips('EURUSD', 0.01, 20, 40);

// SELL with the same geometry
await sugar.sellMarketWithPips('EURUSD', 0.01, 20, 40);

docs.title: 1) Risk-sized, pip-based entry
docs.text:
const lots = await sugar.calculatePositionSize('EURUSD', 1.0, 20);   // 1% over a 20-pip stop
const ticket = await sugar.buyMarketWithPips('EURUSD', lots, 20, 40);  // 1:2 R:R

docs.title: 🔧 Notes
docs.text:
• Pip size is derived from the symbol spec (point × 10 on 3/5-digit symbols).
  • Minimum stop distance still applies — a too-tight pip stop is refused (mqlIntCode 130); check getMinStopLevel().

docs.title: MT4Sugar — Account Information (High-Level API)
docs.text:
The full account snapshot and today's trading summary — the two highest-level account reads.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — over MT4Service.

Implementation: src/MT4Sugar.ts. Demos: examples/demos/sugar/06_sugar_basics.js · 09_sugar_history.js.

← MT4Sugar API Overview

docs.title: 📋 Methods
docs.text:
Method Returns Purpose getAccountInfo() Promise<AccountInfo> Full account snapshot. getDailyStats() Promise<DailyStats> Today's win/loss summary.

AccountInfo = { login, currency, balance, equity, credit, leverage, name, company, server, tradeMode, tradeModeCode, isInvestor, serverTime, utcServerShiftMinutes } (no margin — see Balance & Margin). DailyStats = { totalDeals, winningDeals, losingDeals, winRate, totalProfit, bestDeal, worstDeal }.

docs.title: 📖 Method details
docs.text:
const a = await sugar.getAccountInfo();
console.log(`${a.name} #${a.login} on ${a.server}`);
console.log(`balance ${a.balance.toFixed(2)} ${a.currency}  equity ${a.equity.toFixed(2)}  1:${a.leverage}  ${a.tradeMode}`);

const s = await sugar.getDailyStats();
console.log(`today: ${s.totalDeals} deals, win ${s.winRate.toFixed(1)}%, net ${s.totalProfit.toFixed(2)}`);

docs.title: 1) A one-line status banner
docs.text:
const a = await sugar.getAccountInfo();
console.log(`Acc ${a.login} | ${a.currency} | Bal ${a.balance.toFixed(2)} | Eq ${a.equity.toFixed(2)} | ${a.tradeMode}`);

docs.title: 2) End-of-day report
docs.text:
const s = await sugar.getDailyStats();
console.log(`📊 ${s.winningDeals}/${s.totalDeals} wins, net ${s.totalProfit.toFixed(2)} (best ${s.bestDeal.toFixed(2)}, worst ${s.worstDeal.toFixed(2)})`);

docs.title: 🔧 Notes
docs.text:
• Margin fields aren't in AccountInfo on MT4 — use Balance & Margin (getMargin, live).
  • Deeper stats (profit factor, equity curve) are in the mid layer: service().getTradeStats(from).

docs.title: MT4Sugar — Balance & Margin (High-Level API)
docs.text:
One-liners for account money — balance, equity, margin, free margin, floating profit.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — over MT4Service.

Implementation: src/MT4Sugar.ts. Demos: examples/demos/sugar/06_sugar_basics.js.

← MT4Sugar API Overview

docs.title: 📋 Methods
docs.text:
Method Returns Source getBalance() Promise<number> AccountSummary (cheap). getEquity() Promise<number> AccountSummary (cheap). getProfit() Promise<number> equity − balance. getMargin() Promise<number> live snapshot (OnOpenedOrdersProfit). getFreeMargin() Promise<number> live snapshot. getMarginLevel() Promise<number> live snapshot (percent).

⚠️ Margin on MT4. AccountSummary carries no reliable margin, so getMargin / getFreeMargin / getMarginLevel take one OnOpenedOrdersProfit snapshot (a ~1 s stream read). When the account is flat they fall back to equity (free) / 0. getBalance / getEquity / getProfit are the cheap summary reads.

docs.title: 📖 Method details
docs.text:
console.log('balance', (await sugar.getBalance()).toFixed(2));
console.log('equity ', (await sugar.getEquity()).toFixed(2));
console.log('profit ', (await sugar.getProfit()).toFixed(2));   // floating
console.log('margin ', (await sugar.getMargin()).toFixed(2));   // live snapshot
console.log('free   ', (await sugar.getFreeMargin()).toFixed(2));
console.log('level  ', (await sugar.getMarginLevel()).toFixed(0) + '%');

docs.title: 1) A margin-health check
docs.text:
const level = await sugar.getMarginLevel();   // 0 when flat
if (level > 0 && level < 100)      console.log('⚠️ margin level critical!');
else if (level > 0 && level < 200) console.log('⚠️ low margin level');
else                               console.log('✅ healthy');

docs.title: 2) Affordability before a trade
docs.text:
if ((await sugar.getFreeMargin()) < (await sugar.calculateRequiredMargin('EURUSD', 0.1))) {
  console.log('not enough free margin for 0.1 lots');
}

docs.title: 🔧 Notes
docs.text:
• Minimise live reads — if you need margin repeatedly, subscribe once via service().subscribeOpenedOrdersProfit and read from the callback instead of calling getMargin() in a loop.
  • Floating profit is getProfit() (= equity − balance); per-order profit is in Position Information.

docs.title: MT4Sugar — Prices & Quotes (High-Level API)
docs.text:
One-liners for live prices — bid, ask, spread, a one-shot snapshot, and a price-wait helper.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — over MT4Service.

Implementation: src/MT4Sugar.ts. Demos: examples/demos/sugar/06_sugar_basics.js.

← MT4Sugar API Overview

docs.title: 📋 Methods
docs.text:
Method Returns Purpose getBid(symbol) Promise<number> Latest bid. getAsk(symbol) Promise<number> Latest ask. getSpread(symbol) Promise<number> ask − bid (price units). getPriceInfo(symbol) Promise<PriceInfo> bid / ask / spread-in-pips / time in one snapshot. waitForPrice(symbol, targetBid, timeoutMs?) Promise<PriceInfo \| null> Poll until the bid reaches a target.

PriceInfo = { symbol, bid, ask, spreadPips, time } (time = seconds, server).

docs.title: 📖 Method details
docs.text:
const bid = await sugar.getBid('EURUSD');
const ask = await sugar.getAsk('EURUSD');
console.log('spread', (await sugar.getSpread('EURUSD')).toFixed(5));

const p = await sugar.getPriceInfo('EURUSD');
console.log(`bid ${p.bid} ask ${p.ask} spread ${p.spreadPips.toFixed(1)} pips`);

docs.title: waitForPrice(symbol, targetBid, timeoutMs = 10000)
docs.text:
Polls until the bid reaches targetBid (or returns the next tick when targetBid is 0). Returns the last price, or null on timeout.

const hit = await sugar.waitForPrice('EURUSD', 1.1000, 15000);
console.log(hit ? `reached ${hit.bid}` : 'timed out');

docs.title: 1) A simple price alert
docs.text:
const p = await sugar.waitForPrice('EURUSD', 1.1050, 30000);
if (p) console.log('🔔 EURUSD hit', p.bid);

docs.title: 2) Spread gate before trading
docs.text:
if ((await sugar.getSpread('EURUSD')) > 0.0003) {
  console.log('spread too wide — skipping');
}

docs.title: 🔧 Notes
docs.text:

docs.title: 11 · Trailing Stop
docs.text:
Open one market BUY, then ratchet its stop-loss up as price advances (never down), and close it at the end — "let winners run, cap the downside".

Run: node examples/demos/main.js 11 · File: examples/demos/orchestrators/11_trailing_stop.js · ⚠ opens one live demo order (tiny cfg.testVolume, self-closing).

← Orchestrators Overview

docs.title: 🎯 What it does
docs.text:
A trailing stop keeps a floating stop-loss a fixed distance behind the market. As price rises the stop follows it up; when price falls the stop stays put. This locks in gains while leaving room for the order to keep running — and guarantees an exit if the move reverses.

This orchestrator is the smallest end-to-end example of managing an order over time: open → watch → adjust → close.

docs.title: 🧠 How it works
docs.text:
buyMarket → loop(cycles):
  read bid → wantSL = bid − trailPips·pip
  if wantSL > bestSL: modifyPositionSL(ticket, wantSL)   // raise only
→ closePosition(ticket)
  1. Select & measure. service().symbolSelect(sym, true) then getSymbolInfo for digits/point → compute the pip (point × 10 on 3/5-digit symbols, else point).
  2. Open. buyMarket(sym, cfg.testVolume) returns the ticket (throws on a rejection — e.g. market closed — which the demo catches and reports).
  3. Trail. Each cycle: confirm the order is still open (getPositionByTicket), read the bid, compute wantSL = bid − trailPips·pip, and only raise the stop (if wantSL > bestSL). Raising calls modifyPositionSL(ticket, wantSL).
  4. Close. After the cycles, closePosition(ticket).

Ratchet rule. The stop moves up only (wantSL > bestSL). That's what makes it a trailing stop rather than a stop that drifts with every tick.

docs.title: 🎛️ Options
🔑 Key code
docs.text:
let ticket;
try { ticket = await sugar.buyMarket(sym, cfg.testVolume); }
catch (e) { console.log(`rejected (market closed?): ${e.message}`); return; }

let bestSL = 0;
for (let c = 1; c <= cycles; c++) {
  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, intervalMs));
  const pos = await sugar.getPositionByTicket(ticket);
  if (!pos) return;                       // closed elsewhere
  const bid = await sugar.getBid(sym);
  const wantSL = bid - trailPips * pip;
  if (wantSL > bestSL) {                   // raise only
    bestSL = wantSL;
    await sugar.modifyPositionSL(ticket, bestSL);
  }
}
await sugar.closePosition(ticket);

docs.title: 🔗 Sugar methods used
docs.text: buyMarket · getBid · getSymbolInfo · getPositionByTicket · modifyPositionSL · closePosition.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & adapting it
docs.text:
• Raise-only is the whole point — drop the wantSL > bestSL guard and it's no longer a trailing stop.
  • Market must be open — buyMarket rejects (mqlIntCode 132) out of session; the demo returns gracefully.
  • SELL variant: mirror the geometry — wantSL = ask + trailPips·pip and lower the stop only.
  • Activation threshold: start trailing only once the order is in profit by N pips (compare bid to pos.openPrice).
  • Real use: replace the fixed cycles loop with a tick stream (subscribeQuotes) and no auto-close.

docs.title: 12 · Grid Trader
docs.text:
Lay a symmetric grid of pending orders around price — buy-limits below and sell-limits above, levels each side, stepPips apart — list them, then delete the whole grid.

Run: node examples/demos/main.js 12 · File: examples/demos/orchestrators/12_grid_trader.js · ⚠ places small live pending orders on the demo account and deletes them.

← Orchestrators Overview

docs.title: 🎯 What it does
docs.text: A grid brackets the current price with pending orders at fixed intervals, so a move in either direction triggers entries. This example builds the grid, confirms it's live, and then tears it down — a compact tour of placing and cancelling pending orders.

docs.title: 🧠 How it works
docs.text:
read bid/ask → for each level i:
  buyLimit  @ bid − i·step·pip
  sellLimit @ ask + i·step·pip
→ service().pendingOrders()  (confirm)
→ closePosition(ticket) for each  (deletes the pending)
  1. Select & measure. service().symbolSelect(sym, true), getSymbolInfo for the pip, then getBid / getAsk.
  2. Place. For each level i (1..levels): a buyLimit i steps below the bid and a sellLimit i steps above the ask. Each returns a pending ticket (rejections are caught per order).
  3. Confirm. service().pendingOrders() lists the live pending orders.
  4. Clean up. closePosition(ticket) on each placed ticket — the same call that closes a market order deletes a pending one.

docs.title: 🎛️ Options
docs.text:
Option Default Meaning levels 2 Number of grid levels per side. stepPips 20 Distance between levels, in pips.

cfg.testVolume sets each order's lot size.

await gridTrader(sugar, cfg, { levels: 3, stepPips: 25 });

docs.title: 🔑 Key code
docs.text:
const info = await sugar.getSymbolInfo(sym);
const pip = info.point * (info.digits === 3 || info.digits === 5 ? 10 : 1);
const bid = await sugar.getBid(sym), ask = await sugar.getAsk(sym);

const tickets = [];
for (let i = 1; i <= levels; i++) {
  const below = bid - i * stepPips * pip;
  const above = ask + i * stepPips * pip;
  try { tickets.push(await sugar.buyLimit(sym, cfg.testVolume, below)); } catch (e) { console.log('buyLimit rejected:', e.message); }
  try { tickets.push(await sugar.sellLimit(sym, cfg.testVolume, above)); } catch (e) { console.log('sellLimit rejected:', e.message); }
}

const orders = await sugar.service().pendingOrders();
console.log('pending now live:', orders.length);

for (const t of tickets) { try { await sugar.closePosition(t); } catch { /* already gone */ } }

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & adapting it
docs.text:
• Too close to price? A pending limit inside the stops level is refused (mqlIntCode 130); widen stepPips.
  • Market closed? Nothing places — the demo reports and returns.
  • One-sided grid: place only buyLimits (accumulation) or only sellLimits.
  • Real use: keep the grid live, attach SL/TP to each leg, and re-fill filled levels instead of deleting.

docs.title: 13 · Risk Manager
docs.text:
Each cycle, read account health (equity, margin level, floating P/L, open orders); if drawdown exceeds a limit or the margin level drops too low, close everything — a protective kill-switch.

Run: node examples/demos/main.js 13 · File: examples/demos/orchestrators/13_risk_manager.js · ⛔ read-only until a limit breaks, then it flattens the account.

← Orchestrators Overview

docs.title: 🎯 What it does
docs.text: A risk manager doesn't open trades — it watches the account and acts only when a guardrail is crossed. This example polls equity and margin on a timer, computes drawdown from a starting balance, and triggers closeAllPositions() on a breach.

docs.title: 🧠 How it works
docs.text:
startBalance = getBalance()
loop(cycles):
  equity   = getAccountInfo().equity
  marginLvl= getMarginLevel()          // live snapshot — not in AccountInfo on MT4
  floating = getTotalProfit()
  open     = countOpenPositions()
  ddPct    = (startBalance − equity) / startBalance · 100
  if ddPct > maxDrawdownPct OR (open>0 and marginLvl < minMarginLevel):
    closeAllPositions()   ← kill-switch
    return

⚠️ Margin on MT4. AccountInfo has no margin level, so the Risk Manager reads it with getMarginLevel() (one OnOpenedOrdersProfit snapshot).

docs.title: 🎛️ Options
docs.text:
Option Default Meaning maxDrawdownPct 5 Close everything if equity drops this % below the start balance. minMarginLevel 150 Close everything if the margin level falls below this % (while orders are open). cycles 5 How many times to check. intervalMs 800 Delay between checks, ms. 
await riskManager(sugar, cfg, { maxDrawdownPct: 3, minMarginLevel: 200, cycles: 20 });

docs.title: 🔑 Key code
docs.text:
const startBalance = await sugar.getBalance();

for (let c = 1; c <= cycles; c++) {
  const a = await sugar.getAccountInfo();
  const marginLevel = await sugar.getMarginLevel();      // live
  const floating = await sugar.getTotalProfit();
  const open = await sugar.countOpenPositions();
  const ddPct = startBalance > 0 ? ((startBalance - a.equity) / startBalance) * 100 : 0;

  const breach = ddPct > maxDrawdownPct || (open > 0 && marginLevel > 0 && marginLevel < minMarginLevel);
  if (breach) {
    const closed = await sugar.closeAllPositions();
    console.log(`⚠ LIMIT BREACHED — closed ${closed} positions`);
    return;
  }
  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, intervalMs));
}

docs.title: 🔗 Sugar methods used
docs.text: getBalance · getAccountInfo · getMarginLevel · getTotalProfit / countOpenPositions · closeAllPositions.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & adapting it
docs.text:
• Read-only by design — it only trades (closes) on a breach.
  • getMarginLevel() is a live read (~1 s). For a tight loop, subscribe once via service().subscribeOpenedOrdersProfit and read margin from the callback instead.
  • Add a daily-loss limit: compare getProfitToday() against a floor.
  • Real use: run it continuously (not a fixed cycles), alert on breach (email/Slack) and optionally disable new entries rather than flattening.

docs.title: 14 · Adaptive Preset
docs.text:
A preset coordinates orchestrators behind one decision. It reads recent bars, classifies the market, and dispatches to the matching orchestrator.

← Orchestrators Overview

docs.title: 🎯 What it does
docs.text:
Rather than hard-code one strategy, the preset looks at the last 20 H1 bars, derives two ratios, and chooses:

Market mode Orchestrator Why TRENDING Trailing Stop ride the move RANGING Grid Trader fade the range VOLATILE Risk Manager stay defensive

This shows how one-liners compose not just into a loop, but into a decision that selects a loop.

docs.title: 🧠 How it works
docs.text:
bars = service().lastBars(sym, 'H1', 20)
avgRange = mean(high − low)
trend = |last.close − first.close| / avgRange     (net directional move, in "ranges")
spike = max(high − low) / avgRange                (biggest bar vs typical)

mode = spike > 2.5 ? VOLATILE
     : trend > 2.0 ? TRENDING
     :               RANGING
→ dispatch to the matching orchestrator
  1. Read bars. service().lastBars(sym, 'H1', 20) — the newest 20 H1 candles (no server-time math needed).
  2. Measure. Average bar range, the net move across the window (in units of average range), and the biggest single-bar spike.
  3. Classify & dispatch. A big spike → VOLATILE (risk manager); a strong net move → TRENDING (trailing stop); otherwise RANGING (grid). With too few bars it defaults to the grid.

docs.title: 🔑 Key code
docs.text:
const bars = await sugar.service().lastBars(sym, 'H1', 20);
if (bars.length < 5) return gridTrader(sugar, cfg);

let sumRange = 0, maxRange = 0;
for (const b of bars) { const r = b.high - b.low; sumRange += r; maxRange = Math.max(maxRange, r); }
const avgRange = sumRange / bars.length;
const move = Math.abs(bars[bars.length - 1].close - bars[0].close);
const trend = avgRange > 0 ? move / avgRange : 0;
const spike = avgRange > 0 ? maxRange / avgRange : 1;

const mode = spike > 2.5 ? 'VOLATILE' : trend > 2.0 ? 'TRENDING' : 'RANGING';
if (mode === 'VOLATILE') return riskManager(sugar, cfg);
if (mode === 'TRENDING') return trailingStop(sugar, cfg);
return gridTrader(sugar, cfg);

docs.title: 🔗 Used
docs.text: service().lastBars to read bars, then one of 11 Trailing / 12 Grid / 13 Risk.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & adapting it
docs.text:
• The thresholds are illustrative (spike > 2.5, trend > 2.0) — tune them to your instrument and timeframe.
  • Add indicators: swap the simple range ratios for ATR, ADX, or a moving-average slope for a sharper regime read.
  • Different timeframe: pass another timeframe to lastBars ('M15', 'H4') to react faster or slower.
  • More modes: add a "quiet" mode that does nothing, or a "breakout" mode that only arms pending stops.

docs.title: Orchestrators — Overview
docs.text:
Small, self-contained strategy loops built entirely on MT4Sugar. Each is a plain async function demo(sugar, cfg, opts) you can read, run on the demo account, and adapt.

These are teaching examples of coordinating the SDK over time — not production trading systems. They show how the one-liners compose into a working loop.

docs.title: 🧩 Orchestrator vs preset
docs.text:
• An orchestrator runs one strategy end-to-end (open → manage → close, or monitor → act).
  • A preset picks which orchestrator to run from the current market conditions, then delegates to it.

So the three orchestrators are the strategies; the preset is the coordinator on top.

docs.title: 📁 What's here
docs.text:
# File Idea Writes trades? 11 Trailing Stop Open a BUY, ratchet its SL up as price advances, close. ✅ one order 12 Grid Trader Lay a symmetric grid of pending limits, list, delete. ✅ pending orders 13 Risk Manager Monitor equity / margin / drawdown; kill-switch on breach. ⛔ read-only unless a limit breaks 14 Adaptive Preset Classify the market, dispatch to the matching orchestrator. ↪ delegates

The numbering follows the demo files (examples/demos/orchestrators/, .../presets/).

docs.title: How the preset composes them
docs.text:
┌──────────────── 14 Adaptive Preset ───────────────┐

                 │                 VOLATILE → 13 Risk Manager        │
                 └───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: 🧱 The shape they share
docs.text:
module.exports = async function demo(sugar, cfg, opts = {}) {
  // sugar : a connected MT4Sugar
  // cfg   : { testSymbol, testVolume, ... }  (from examples/demos/config)
  // opts  : per-run tuning (cycles, pips, thresholds…)
};
  • sugar — a connected MT4Sugar; reach down with sugar.service() / sugar.account().
  • cfg — testSymbol and testVolume drive what and how much; shared across demos.
  • opts — each orchestrator documents its own knobs (trail distance, grid levels, risk limits…).

Run any of them from the demo menu:

node examples/demos/main.js 11      # trailing stop
node examples/demos/main.js 12      # grid trader
node examples/demos/main.js 13      # risk manager
node examples/demos/main.js 14      # adaptive preset

docs.title: 🧠 Shared building blocks
docs.text:
All four lean on the same handful of sugar calls:

Concern Sugar methods Price & spec getBid / getAsk · getSymbolInfo · service().lastBars Enter buyMarket / buyLimit / sellLimit Manage modifyPositionSL · closePosition / closeAllPositions Watch getAccountInfo · getMarginLevel · getTotalProfit / countOpenPositions / getPositionByTicket

The pip convention is shared too: pip = point × (digits is 3 or 5 ? 10 : 1).

MT4 note: a "position" is an open market order (by ticket). Live margin isn't in the account summary — the Risk Manager reads it via getMarginLevel() (a live snapshot).

docs.title: ⚠️ Safety
docs.text: 11, 12 and 14 place live orders on the configured demo account (tiny cfg.testVolume, self-closing). 13 is read-only until a risk limit is breached, at which point it closes everything. Never point these at a real account while learning.
